PROGRAM: swarm-context-graph (program-triage-2026-10-17; pins in triage-2026-10-17/PINS.txt; shard requirements/swarm-context-graph-requirements.md; dossier triage/swarm-context-graph-dossier.md; audit requirements/RELEASE-CLAIMS-AUDIT.md).

STATEMENT: When result.observations carries any row that is not a fresh observed value — replayed===true, or freshness==='reused', or degraded===true, or a status outside the pin's observed-value set {observed, null} (including any unknown word) — the RF reader adapter shall project coverage 'partial' and a statusTone other than 'success', with one note naming the row count, the reused/replayed count and the verbatim status words; all-fresh rows, observations [] or absent keep today's output byte-identical.

RATIONALE: Dossier G5 (CONFIRMED-GAP observations-rows-reused-not-current): SCG-R024 (01-PRODUCT-AND-REQUIREMENTS.md:37@8a8b83e4d), ADR-SCG-008 (09-ADRS-AND-DECISIONS.md:26-27), 11-SKILL-AND-LX-DELIVERY.md:13 (freshness witnesses, not model conjecture), 04-CLI-AND-SCHEMAS.md:94 (replayed = host projection of reuse; freshness = host witness). The key rides every pinned render (render_service.py:1513@8a8b83e4d); pin vocabulary status observed|missing|null|suppressed|invalid|timeout|nonzero|truncated|denied, freshness captured_at_render|reused, replayed and degraded booleans (context.render.schema.json:1071-1082,:1112-1152@8a8b83e4d; observed-value statuses domain/observation.py:100). Pi computes clean = live && !flagged && !overBudget without reading rows (reactivefiber-observer.ts:187-198@9df9a03) and the projection stamps freshness 'current' from connection state (observation.ts:588) — a reused or denied row on an ok, zero-error envelope reads complete/success/current today; the one gap that mislabels evidence at the pin, hence P0. Correction carried: the program's reused/stale_inputs status words (03-LOW-LEVEL-DESIGN.md:44) are a planned migration, not the pin's enum.

ACCEPTANCE: ["RED on 9df9a03, it.each over three rows on an otherwise clean rf-cli envelope: (a) {observation_id:'rfl_…', lens_key:'beads.current', value_digest:'sha256:…', status:'observed', code:null, freshness:'reused', replayed:true, required:true, degraded:false, persisted:true}; (b) {…, status:'denied', code:'RF_OBSERVATION_DENIED', freshness:'captured_at_render', replayed:false, degraded:true}; (c) {…, status:'stale_inputs', freshness:'captured_at_render', replayed:false, degraded:false} — each asserts coverage==='partial', statusTone!=='success', a note matching /observations: 1 row/ naming reused/replayed for (a) and the verbatim status word for (b),(c); HEAD projects complete/success for all three.", "Positive controls: observations [], absent, and one row {status:'observed', freshness:'captured_at_render', replayed:false, degraded:false} leave the clean R1 expectation toStrictEqual unchanged except, for the fresh row, one added note 'observations: 1 row, 0 reused'.", "Contradiction fences (schema :1140,:1144): replayed:true with freshness 'captured_at_render', replayed:false with freshness 'reused', degraded:true with status 'observed' → refused 'validation'; a row missing status/freshness/replayed or a non-array observations → 'validation' (observer) / 'transport' (provider).", "Projection effect: after ObservationProjection.refresh the node's completeness==='partial'; the adapter writes no projection freshness field (freshness semantics stay projection-owned; the note is the row-level witness).", 'Gate: default gate (fixture keys from R11).']

title: W16-C: pure bounded workflow_catalog and workflow_inspect reply builders over the capability registry policy surface (filter/limit/cursor pagination, exact discover:/inspect: grant ACL, compact bounded sanitized JSON, never implicit invocation); Pi tool registration excluded
description:
Gap (groomed at rig HEAD 1fc74f0, branch workbench/implementation-program): wb-69g (W16) spans workflow_catalog/inspect/validate/execute/observe/control/compare, but its only children cover workflow_control decisions (wb-69g.1) and the workflow_observe reply builder (wb-752.2). Nothing covers the catalog/inspect reply half, and docs/workbench/15 W16 acceptance is "compact bounded result and ACL".

Scope (atomic, pure, hot-file free): a new pure module (suggested src/workbench/tool-replies.ts or sibling-consistent location) exporting buildWorkflowCatalogReply(registrySnapshot, grants, {filter?, limit?, cursor?}) and buildWorkflowInspectReply(registrySnapshot, grants, target, view?) that return compact bounded sanitized JSON reply objects for the Pi tools, plus a red-first vitest. ACL is exact-string and deny-by-default: a capability id without discover:<capabilityId> in the grant set is absent from the catalog reply (absent, not an error row); an inspect reply requires inspect:<capabilityId> AND an advertised, implemented inspect mode, else an explicit typed unavailable. Cursor pagination is stable; a byte cap truncates with a visible marker and offered-vs-returned counts; every string field routes through the shared sanitizers in src/workbench/redaction.ts. The builders perform no invocation and no RPC.

Out of scope: Pi tool registration in src/index.ts (parent slice), observation-backed inspect views (wb-752.2 owns workflow_observe), workflow_validate/execute/control/compare, and ALL W17 hot-reservation files (src/workbench/designer.ts, test/workbench-designer.test.ts, test/workbench-pi-designer.test.ts, workflow_compare surfacing in src/index.ts).
acceptance_criteria:
Red-first: the new vitest fails before the builder module exists. Base 1fc74f0 or later. All quotes are from docs/workbench in the rig (branch workbench/implementation-program).

A1. Catalog shape and pagination. buildWorkflowCatalogReply honors filter/limit/cursor with a stable cursor, enforces a byte cap with a visible truncation marker and offered-vs-returned counts, and returns compact structured JSON only. Quote docs/workbench/11-designer-and-operator.md section "First public Pi tools (proposed)": "workflow_catalog(filter?,limit?,cursor?): saved script sources, MechanicalWorkflows entrypoints, available SDK capabilities and contract references." Quote same section: "Use compact structured schema, discover more capability detail on demand; do not insert all SDK method signatures into every Pi prompt."

A2. ACL exact-string, deny-by-default. A capability whose id lacks discover:<capabilityId> in the grant set is absent from the catalog reply; inspect requires inspect:<capabilityId> plus an advertised, implemented inspect mode, else a typed explicit unavailable; discovery never implies invoke. Quote docs/workbench/06-capability-registry.md section "Current experimental policy surface": "Catalog discovery independently requires exact `discover:<capabilityId>`. Optional provider inspection requires `inspect:<capabilityId>` and an advertised, implemented inspect mode." Quote same section: "Registered descriptors do not grant access." Quote docs/workbench/15-implementation-program.md section "Work breakdown and dependencies" W16 row acceptance: "compact bounded result and ACL".

A3. Inspect never invokes. buildWorkflowInspectReply is pure over its inputs, performs no invocation and no RPC; unknown target or view yields a typed explicit error reply, never a guess. Quote docs/workbench/11-designer-and-operator.md section "First public Pi tools (proposed)": "workflow_inspect(target,view?): definition/source, static projection, native reference/evidence, operation details, never implicit invocation."

A4. Sanitization and falsifiers. Every string field routes through the shared sanitizers in src/workbench/redaction.ts (invariant); offline falsifiers: an empty grant set yields zero catalog rows; a crafted capability title containing an ESC control character is sanitized in the reply; a cursor past the end returns an empty page, not an error; an oversized snapshot triggers the visible truncation marker.

A5. Exclusions and gate. No edits to src/index.ts or any W17 hot-reservation file; ./node_modules/.bin/biome check --write on touched files; npm run typecheck clean (no any, no inline imports); vitest green; existing tests never weakened or deleted.

title: W15-B/VC-5: pure timeline lane model over observed source intervals and native-confirmed ownership/grouping edges (lanes per owner or provider, open intervals stay open, measured concurrency, zoom/pan cell math, clock and gap notes); inspector wiring excluded
description:
Gap (measured at rig HEAD 1fc74f0, branch workbench/implementation-program): src/ui/workflow-inspector.ts:177-191 renders the timeline view as one flat line per viewport node: a bar `(ascii?'#':'━').repeat(Math.max(1,Math.min(20,Math.floor(duration/1000*state.zoom)-state.pan)))` computed only when node.interval has both startedAt and endedAt, otherwise the literal 'timing unavailable (no complete source interval)', closed by the constant 'Waiting/blocked/executing lanes unavailable without producer interval kinds.' No lane grouping exists (the furnace-confirmed Run->Attempt ownership edges that wb-752.1 landed at e797a84 are never consulted by the timeline), no concurrency is measured, an open interval (startedAt without endedAt, which ObservationProjection keeps as-is, test/workbench-observation.test.ts:128) is reported as unavailable instead of open, and the zoom/pan arithmetic lives untested inside the renderer (test/workbench-inspector.test.ts:103 only checks that pan changes the line). docs/workbench/10 § "Four views" (Timeline) requires "relative interval lanes grouped by owner/phase/provider, zoom and horizontal pan, observed waiting/executing/blocked periods and concurrency. Never infer exact timing from text or assume clocks agree; note uncertain clocks or event gaps." ObservationProjection already exposes every read needed: window({scope,invocationId,offset,limit}) -> {nodes,total,revision} with ObservedNode.interval {startedAt,endedAt?} (src/workbench/observation.ts:448), relations({scope,to,limit}) returning incoming typed edges with provenance (:397) and relationRevision() (:467). wb-6ze.1 (in progress) owns workflow-inspector.ts for the overview tree and graph fan-out and leaves the timeline branch untouched; wb-6ze.2 adds ancestor counts in observation.ts; wb-6ze.4 ranks bottlenecks and estimates a critical path. None of them computes lanes, concurrency or the zoom/pan window.

Scope (atomic, pure, hot-file free): ONE new source file src/workbench/timeline.ts and ONE new test file test/workbench-timeline.test.ts; register and wire nothing; do not edit src/ui/workflow-inspector.ts (wb-6ze.1 in flight), src/workbench/observation.ts (wb-6ze.2), src/workbench/designer.ts (reserved 07:00Z), src/index.ts or src/ui/workflow-dialog.ts.

• export const TIMELINE_CONTRACT = 'workbench.timeline/v1'; export type TimelineReader = Pick<ObservationProjection,'window'|'relations'|'relationRevision'>.
• export interface TimelineRequest { scope: ObservationScope; invocationId: string; offset: number; limit: number (1..100, the window cap); zoom: number (safe integer 1..8, cells per second); pan: number (safe integer >= 0, cells); columns: number (safe integer 8..200, bar cells); maxLanes?: number (1..64, default 16); maxRowsPerLane?: number (1..100, default 40); relationLimit?: number (1..100, default 40) }. Invalid values throw CapabilityError('validation') before any reader call.
• export function buildTimelineLanes(reader: TimelineReader, request: TimelineRequest): TimelineModel — pure, synchronous, deterministic (no Date.now, Math.random, process or environment reads; every timestamp comes from reader rows), calls reader.window exactly once and reader.relations at most once per returned node with {scope, to: node.key, limit: relationLimit}; never calls ingest/refresh/relate/markStale or any provider; returns a deeply frozen plain object that survives JSON round-trip losslessly.
• TimelineModel { contract; revision; topologyRevision; origin: { startedAt: string; basis: 'earliest-observed-start' } | { startedAt: null; basis: 'none' }; span: { ms: number | null; complete: boolean }; lanes: readonly TimelineLane[]; concurrency: { maxMeasured: number; basis: 'source-intervals-only'; countsOpenIntervals: true }; notes: readonly TimelineNote[]; truncated: { lanes: boolean; rows: boolean; relations: boolean; window: boolean } }.
• TimelineLane { key: string; label: string; basis: 'ownership' | 'grouping' | 'provider'; confirmed: boolean; rows: readonly TimelineRow[] }. Lane assignment per row: an incoming 'ownership' edge from a node in the same scope -> lane key = that parent's key, basis 'ownership'; else an incoming 'grouping' edge -> that parent's key, basis 'grouping'; else lane key `provider:${nativeRef.provider}`, basis 'provider'. When several parents of the chosen kind qualify, the lexicographically smallest parent key wins and note 'multiple-parents' is added; 'dependency', 'causation' and 'hypothesis' edges never assign a lane or alter timing. confirmed is true only when every edge used for the lane carries provenance.nativeConfirmationRef. Lane label is the parent's presentation.title (redactWorkbenchText then stripUnsafeText, max 80) when the parent is inside the window, else the sanitized parent key, else the provider name.
• TimelineRow { key; nativeRef; title (sanitized, max 80); tone: Presentation['statusTone']; freshness; timing: { kind: 'closed'; startedAt; endedAt; durationMs } | { kind: 'open'; startedAt } | { kind: 'unavailable'; reason: 'no-source-interval' }; bar: { offsetCells; lengthCells; clippedLeft; clippedRight; openEnded } | null }. No field named elapsedMs, estimatedEndedAt or progressPercent exists anywhere in the model.
• Ordering: lanes by earliest row startedAt then key; rows inside a lane by startedAt then key; rows without an interval last, by key. Rows beyond maxRowsPerLane and lanes beyond maxLanes are dropped with truncated.rows / truncated.lanes true; truncated.window is total > offset + returned; truncated.relations is true when any relations page returned exactly relationLimit rows.

- OBSERVE_CONTRACT = "workbench.observe/v1"; type ObserveReader = Pick<ObservationProjection, "window" | "relations" | "events" | "relationRevision" | "stats">.
- interface ObserveRequest { scope: ObservationScope; invocationId: string; cursor?: string; limit?: number (1..40, default 20); selectors?: { tone?: Presentation["statusTone"]; kind?: string; relations?: boolean; events?: { limit: number (1..40) } }; maxBytes?: number (1024..65536, default 16384) }.
- observeInvocation(reader: ObserveReader, request: ObserveRequest): ObserveReply, pure and synchronous: calls only reader methods (window once per call; relations at most once per returned node with limit <= 40 when selectors.relations; events once when selectors.events); never ingest/refresh/relate/markStale, never a provider.
- ObserveReply (frozen plain data, JSON round-trip lossless): { contract; invocationId; window: { offset; limit; returned; total; revision; nextCursor: string | null; truncated: boolean }; nodes: ObserveNode[] where ObserveNode = { key; nativeRef; kind; presentation (title and statusText passed through sanitizeWorkbenchText(value, 200) from src/workbench/redaction.ts; statusTone kept BESIDE statusText, never replacing it); freshness; completeness; sourceConnectionState; observedAt; lastConfirmedAt?; subjectBasis?; interval?; evidenceRefs (each sanitized, at most 20) ; evidenceTruncated: boolean }, never payloadRef bodies or event payloads; relations?: { perNode: { key; outgoing: Record<RelationKind, number>; partial: boolean }[]; basis: "returned-window-only" }; events?: { returned; truncated; completeness: "complete" | "partial-gap"; kinds: Record<string, number>; providers: string[] } (metadata only: no event bodies, no node presentation copies); freshness: { current; stale; unknown; lastKnownRunningStale: number; summary: string } where lastKnownRunningStale counts returned nodes with statusTone "active" and freshness !== "current" and summary contains the literal "last-known-running + stale" whenever that count is > 0, otherwise "all returned nodes current" or "N stale / M unknown"; anomalies: { disconnectedProviders: string[]; partialCompleteness: number; eventGap: boolean; noRelationsAvailable: boolean }; aggregates: "not-wired" (literal until the ancestor-aggregate read model of wb-6ze.2 is wired by a later bead; no estimated numbers); countsBasis: "returned-window"; bytes: number; truncatedForBytes: boolean }.
- Cursor: opaque base64url of JSON { v: 1; offset; invocationId }, validated on decode; a malformed, negative, non-integer, cross-invocation or oversize (> 256 bytes) cursor throws CapabilityError("validation") from src/workbench/capability-registry.ts, never a silent restart at offset 0; nextCursor is null when offset + returned >= total.
- Byte cap: the reply is measured as Buffer.byteLength(JSON.stringify(reply)); when over maxBytes, trim in this deterministic order - events, then relations, then nodes from the tail (adjusting window.returned/truncated and nextCursor so the dropped nodes are reachable on the next page) - and set truncatedForBytes true; never drop freshness, anomalies or window fields.
- No ANSI/control characters anywhere: JSON.stringify(reply) never matches /[\u0000-\u001f\u007f\\u202E\\u200B]/ after sanitization.

1. qa/workbench/live-adverse-receipt.mjs (new, pure, no src/ or dist/ import): assessAdverseJourneys(observed) -> { findings: {rule, detail}[], realised: boolean } and buildAdverseReceipt(input) -> frozen plain object { contract: "workbench.claude-adverse/v1", utc, revision, node, arch, platform, sdkVersion, model, journeys, sdkEventTypes, findings, realised, pass }. "claude-opus-5-5", tools: [], settingSources: [], permissionMode: "dontAsk", onMessage, onSettled}).

title: W22-B: packed npm artifact boundary falsifier (top-level allowlist, agent-tooling denylist, bundled-only node_modules, .npmignore fix for tracked .agents/ and .codex/) plus evidence-grade package-smoke receipt (revision, toolchain, host, pack determinism)
description:
Gap (measured at rig HEAD ad3cf6e908f0, branch workbench/implementation-program): `npm pack --dry-run --ignore-scripts --json` packs 374 files including the git-tracked agent-tooling files `.agents/skills/beads/SKILL.md`, `.agents/skills/beads/agents/openai.yaml`, `.codex/config.toml` and `.codex/hooks.json`. `.codex/hooks.json` wires `bd codex-hook` commands to SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit/PreCompact/PostCompact, so a consumer who opens the installed package directory in Codex inherits hook commands from the npm artifact. `.npmignore` already excludes `.pi`, `.claude`, `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` under its own heading "Internal contributor/agent instructions — not for distribution" but omits `.agents/` and `.codex/`. qa/workbench/package-smoke.mjs (default forge gate step `package-smoke`) denies only the `.beads/` and `.forge/` prefixes, and its receipt `{contract:"workbench.package-smoke/v1", fileCount, sha, integrity, privateStateIncluded}` records no revision, tool versions, timestamp, host or command, contrary to the docs/workbench/14 truth-label rule. Packed `node_modules/` content is today exactly the three `inBundle: true` package-lock entries (@forge/sdk 49 files, @furnace/sdk 79, @hyperunix/sdk 111); nothing asserts that.

Scope (atomic, hot-file free, no src/ edits):
1. `.npmignore`: add `.agents/` and `.codex/` under the existing "Internal contributor/agent instructions" heading. Change nothing else (qa/, docs/, examples/ keep shipping as today; see notes).
2. `qa/workbench/package-boundary.mjs` (new, plain ESM, no dependencies): export TOP_LEVEL_ALLOWLIST (LICENSE, README.md, CHANGELOG.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md, package.json, forge.toml, dist, src, docs, examples, qa, vendor, node_modules), DENIED_PREFIXES (.agents/, .codex/, .pi/, .claude/, .beads/, .forge/, .furnace/, .hyperunix/, .reactive-fiber/, .github/, machines/, test/, tests/), DENIED_BASENAMES (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, biome.json, tsconfig.json), DENIED_PATTERNS (basename matches /\.jsonl$/, /^vitest\..*config\.ts$/ or /\.test\.ts$/), `classifyPackedPaths(paths, { bundledLockEntries })` returning `{ violations: {path, rule}[], topLevel: string[] }` where a `node_modules/` path is a violation unless its (scope-aware) package name is in bundledLockEntries (the package-lock `packages` entry names whose `inBundle === true`), and a pure `buildPackageReceipt(input)` that assembles the v2 receipt from already-measured values.
3. `qa/workbench/package-smoke.mjs`: keep every existing v1 assertion verbatim; add classifyPackedPaths over the pack listing (any violation fails the smoke listing every offending path and rule); pack the same tree a second time and assert identical `shasum` and `integrity`; emit receipt `contract: "workbench.package-smoke/v2"` with the v1 fields plus revision (`git rev-parse HEAD`, or the literal `unknown:not-a-git-checkout`), dirty (true/false from `git status --porcelain`, or null when revision is unknown), node (process.version), npm (`npm --version`), platform, arch, utc, command, topLevel (sorted), bundled (sorted lock entry names), denied (always [] on success).
4. `test/workbench-package-boundary.test.ts` (new vitest; no npm child process, no network): imports the classifier and receipt builder from `../qa/workbench/package-boundary.mjs`, runs the fixture cases in acceptance item 6, unit-tests the receipt builder with fake git results, and parses `.npmignore` asserting the required exclusion lines.

Out of scope (flag in the ledger line, do not change): whether `qa/` development runners and `docs/` should ship; a package.json `exports` map; version bump; npm publication; editing docs/TRACEABILITY.md or docs/workbench/*; forge.toml. If any step needs a hot file or a src/ change, stop and return blocked.

Files: .npmignore; qa/workbench/package-smoke.mjs; qa/workbench/package-boundary.mjs (new); test/workbench-package-boundary.test.ts (new).

title: W13/VC-2: Forge gate-status reader adapter projects NativeSnapshots and grouping edges (historical last_result stays unknown/partial, failed gate stays failed); tool wiring excluded
description:
Gap: the only NativeSnapshot producer in src/ is FurnaceObserver.projectionSnapshot (src/workbench/furnace-observer.ts, extended by wb-752.1); grep -rn "NativeSnapshot\|projectionSnapshot" src returns only that file and its hot consumer src/index.ts:2560. The real native Forge read (src/workbench/providers/forge.ts, invoke() result {contract:'forge.gate.status/v1', protocolMethod:'gate.status', source}) never reaches the ObservationProjection or the inspector. docs/workbench/09 § Reader adapters requires a read-current-snapshot function per supported provider, and docs/workbench/15 gates the P1 inspector release on "real native source". The measured native read of this workspace returned status=success with authoritative_current=false, which must appear as historical/indeterminate, never as a verified PASS.

Scope (atomic, additive, new file, hot-file free): src/workbench/forge-observer.ts exporting
- forgeGateTopology(reading: JsonValue, context: { scope: ObservationScope; target: string; capturedAt: string; observedAt: string; invocationId?: string }): { snapshots: NativeSnapshot[]; relations: ForgeObservedRelation[]; diagnostics: string[] } where ForgeObservedRelation is exactly the parameter type of ObservationProjection.relate.
- Validation: reading must be the exact provider output (contract 'forge.gate.status/v1', protocolMethod 'gate.status', source.envelope.reason_code string, source.data.packages an array of objects with a string ref of at most 256 bytes and no control characters); anything else throws CapabilityError('validation'). Unknown extra producer fields are tolerated, never required and never copied into presentation text.
- One workspace snapshot: source {provider:'forge', type:'gate-status', id:'workspace', scope: context.target}, kind 'forge.gate.status.snapshot', node.type 'sdk-operation', statusText built from source.status, envelope.verdict and envelope.reason_code (e.g. "partial · COULD_NOT_JUDGE · FORGE_GATE_INCOMPLETE · verification indeterminate"), statusTone 'unknown' unless every package is authoritative_current === true (then 'failure' if any last_result === 'failure', 'success' only if all last_result === 'success'), coverage 'partial' when source.status !== 'success' or any package is not authoritative_current, otherwise 'complete'; sourceVersion 'forge.gate.status/v1'; evidenceRefs ['forge:gate.status:<reason_code>'].
- One snapshot per package: source {provider:'forge', type:'gate-status', id: pkg.ref, scope: context.target}, statusText "<last_result> (historical; authoritative_current=false[; <unverified_reason>])" with statusTone 'unknown' whenever authoritative_current !== true; when authoritative_current === true, statusText "<last_result> (current)" with statusTone 'success' for last_result 'success', 'failure' for 'failure', 'unknown' otherwise. Never an interval (Forge gate status carries no timestamps), never subjectBasis (a target path is not a basis), never definitionDigest.
- One 'grouping' relation workspace->package per package with provenance {source:'forge-observer', observedAt: context.observedAt}; never 'ownership' (the gate.status envelope carries no native lifecycle confirmation reference, and relate() rejects ownership without one) and never 'dependency'/'causation'/'hypothesis'.
- All presentation text passes redactWorkbenchText (import from src/workbench/redaction.ts, hot — do not edit) and is bounded to 200 characters so ObservationProjection.refresh never throws on producer text.

Out of scope: registering or wiring the adapter into furnace_observe/workflow_observe (src/index.ts, hot), providers/forge.ts changes (the adapter consumes its output), inspector text assertions or changes (wb-6ze.1 owns src/ui/workflow-inspector.ts this round), any Forge write or gate.run.
Files: src/workbench/forge-observer.ts (new); test/workbench-forge-observer.test.ts (new). Fixture: reuse the SOURCE shape from test/workbench-forge-contract.test.ts.
acceptance_criteria:
Red-first: test/workbench-forge-observer.test.ts fails before src/workbench/forge-observer.ts exists. Quotes are from docs/workbench in the rig (branch workbench/implementation-program).

F1 Historical result is not a verdict. With SOURCE = {status:'success', envelope:{verdict:null, reason_code:'FORGE_OK'}, data:{packages:[{ref:'code:pi-subagents', last_result:'success', authoritative_current:false, unverified_reason:'FORGE_CURRENT_STATE_UNVERIFIED'}]}} wrapped as {contract:'forge.gate.status/v1', protocolMethod:'gate.status', source: SOURCE}: exactly two snapshots; the package snapshot has statusTone 'unknown', statusText containing 'historical', 'authoritative_current=false' and 'FORGE_CURRENT_STATE_UNVERIFIED', coverage 'partial'; JSON.stringify(result) does not contain '"statusTone":"success"'. Quote docs/workbench/00-current-state-and-source-map.md § "2026-10-15 implementation update (experimental; evidence-scoped)": "authoritative_current=false (historical status, not current verification). That latter field is preserved without a fabricated PASS." Quote docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-015: "Workbench cannot turn absent/unknown/partial producer evidence into successful domain verdict."

F2 Failed gate stays failed; current success is success. authoritative_current true with last_result 'failure' -> package statusTone 'failure' and workspace statusTone 'failure' even though source.status is 'success'; authoritative_current true with last_result 'success' -> 'success' and coverage 'complete'. Quote docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Acceptance/negative controls" item 7: "A true Forge failed gate remains failed despite transport success." Quote docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md § "Matrix by subsystem" Forge row: "gate on exact candidate/basis with producer verdict | source basis changed -> no PASS".

F3 Partial envelope is indeterminate, not empty success. {status:'partial', envelope:{verdict:'COULD_NOT_JUDGE', reason_code:'FORGE_GATE_INCOMPLETE'}, data:{packages:[]}} -> one workspace snapshot with statusTone 'unknown', statusText containing 'COULD_NOT_JUDGE' and 'indeterminate', coverage 'partial', zero package snapshots, zero relations, and one diagnostic naming the empty package list. Quote docs/workbench/19-worked-examples.md § "Example H: native evidence refusal": "Pi must show \"verification indeterminate\", not success, even if host RPC returned normally and text says \"build completed\"."

F4 Contract validation fails closed. contract 'hyperunix.find/v1', protocolMethod 'gate.run', missing envelope.reason_code, packages not an array, a package without a string ref, or a ref longer than 256 bytes each throw CapabilityError with category 'validation'; an extra unknown field on a package or the envelope is tolerated and never appears in any statusText. Quote docs/workbench/13-contracts-and-config.md § "Key validations": "unrecognized SDK message version => diagnostic rather than silent success." Quote docs/workbench/06-capability-registry.md § "Registration and resolution": "validate output representation without erasing unknown producer fields."

F5 Only grouping edges, no invented lifecycle or timing. Every relation has kind 'grouping' and provenance.source 'forge-observer'; relations.length === packages.length; no snapshot carries interval, subjectBasis or definitionDigest. Quote docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Relationships are typed and provenanced": "lifecycle ownership (only if native producer confirms)" and "grouping only (phase, display scope)". Quote docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md § "Four views" Timeline: "Never infer exact timing from text or assume clocks agree; note uncertain clocks or event gaps." Quote test/workbench-native-evidence.test.ts case title: "preserves Forge native operation and partial status but never workspace path as basis".

F6 Read-model integration. Applying snapshots via ObservationProjection.refresh and relations via relate on a real projection: query({scope, parent: workspaceRef, limit: 10}) returns exactly the package nodes; query({scope, statusTone:'unknown', limit: 10}) includes the historical package; every relations({scope, from: workspaceKey}) entry is 'grouping'; a second forgeGateTopology call with the same reading and a later observedAt refreshes without duplicating nodes (stats().nodes unchanged). Quote docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Reader adapters": "Reader adapter returns snapshot {nativeRef, capturedAt, observedAt, sourceRevision?, coverage?, nativePayloadRef}". Quote docs/workbench/15-implementation-program.md § "Gating policy": "P1 inspector release requires VC-4/VC-5 with real native source and scale benchmark."

F7 Bounded, redacted presentation. A reason_code of 10,000 characters containing 'Bearer abc123' and '\x1b[31m' yields statusText of at most 200 characters with no control characters, containing '[REDACTED]' and not 'abc123', and refresh() does not throw. Quote docs/workbench/12-security.md § "Input and output hardening": "Validate Unicode and terminal escape sequences before display (no untrusted ANSI injection)." Quote docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Acceptance/negative controls" item 10: "Large/secret payload does not leak into Pi tool result or screen by default."

F8 Native status is not replaced by tone. statusText always contains the literal native last_result / verdict strings; the test asserts that native 'success' and tone 'unknown' coexist in the F1 package snapshot. Quote docs/workbench/13-contracts-and-config.md § "Observation projection": "Do not replace native status with presentation.statusTone. This is a read model only."

F9 Gate: ./node_modules/.bin/biome check --write on touched files; npm run typecheck clean (no any, no inline imports); ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run test/workbench-forge-observer.test.ts test/workbench-forge-contract.test.ts test/workbench-native-evidence.test.ts test/workbench-observation.test.ts green; existing tests untouched; record red and green commands in the delivered ledger line; do not edit docs/TRACEABILITY.md (acceptance owner reconciles).

Preserve authoritative_current semantics: historical green never presented as current verification; transport success never PASS; outputs route through shared sanitizers (src/workbench/redaction.ts). Base on ad3cf6e+.

Two added files only; relay gate PASS cmd_e486eef99aac with 15/15 mutation sweep; my independent isolated-worktree complete gate PASS against the current tip (receipt /tmp/pi-land-6hb2-gate.json), exercising the adapter together with the landed forge-operation evidence-ref behaviour.

title: W14/VC-5: Incremental ancestor aggregates over observed grouping/ownership edges in ObservationProjection (measured counts, interval envelope, incomplete-trace label; inspector wiring excluded)
description:
Gap: ObservationProjection (src/workbench/observation.ts) keeps flat per-node indexes (status, kind, basis, evidence, version, time) but no ancestor aggregate: nothing answers "how many observed children/descendants does this group or Run have, in which status tones, with which interval envelope" without re-walking relations per frame. docs/workbench/10 requires ancestor aggregates to be maintained incrementally and the overview to show "status and counts"; docs/workbench/09 § Aggregates and profiling requires measured counts with an explicit "incomplete trace" label instead of a precise critical path. wb-9x5.2 (W21-A, seat g1) explicitly deferred "adding ancestor/supernode aggregation to observation.ts or workflow-inspector.ts" to a follow-up; wb-6ze.1 (W15 nested tree) is confined to the inspector and uses no new projection API. This bead supplies the read-model half only.

Scope (atomic, additive, hot-file free), all inside src/workbench/observation.ts:
- export interface AncestorAggregate { key: string; revision: number; topologyRevision: number; direct: { children: number; settled: number; byTone: Record<Presentation["statusTone"], number> }; descendants: { counted: number; byTone: Record<Presentation["statusTone"], number>; stale: number; depthReached: number; truncated: boolean }; intervals: { known: number; missing: number; open: number; earliestStartedAt?: string; latestEndedAt?: string }; trace: "incomplete" | "bounded"; criticalPath: "unestablished"; basis: "observed-grouping-ownership" }
- aggregate(filter: { scope: ObservationScope; key: string }): AncestorAggregate | undefined — a copied value; undefined for unknown or cross-scope keys without any traversal.
- aggregateStats(): { adjustments: number; rebuilds: number; maxVisitedPerUpdate: number } (additive; the existing stats() shape {nodes, events, edges} is unchanged).
Child edges are outgoing relations of kind 'grouping' or 'ownership' (parent = from, child = to). Set semantics: a descendant is counted once per ancestor even through diamonds. Depth cap AGGREGATE_DEPTH = 8 (same cap as wb-6ze.1); cycles terminate at the first repeated key. 'dependency', 'causation' and 'hypothesis' edges never trigger or contribute. Hot path: a node's status/interval/freshness change (ingest, refresh, markStale, disconnect, reconnect) adjusts its ancestors by walking incoming grouping/ownership edges with a per-walk visited set — O(depth x fan-in), never a scan of nodes or events. Topology changes (relate/removeEdge of grouping/ownership edges, discard/eviction) rebuild only the affected ancestors from their bounded subtree. settled = success + failure tones; stale = descendants whose freshness !== 'current'; intervals use source intervals only (earliest startedAt, latest endedAt; an open interval increments open and never fabricates an end); trace is 'incomplete' whenever intervals.missing > 0 or descendants.truncated; criticalPath is the literal 'unestablished' (no number, no estimate, no token or cost fields).

Out of scope: rendering counts in src/ui/workflow-inspector.ts (reserved this round by wb-6ze.1 and wb-g1g.1; a later bead wires overview counts), workflow_observe tool output (src/index.ts, hot), supernode collapse, concurrency/critical-path profiling, any cap change.
Files: src/workbench/observation.ts (edit, additive); test/workbench-observation-aggregates.test.ts (new). test/workbench-observation*.test.ts, test/workbench-projection-invalidation.test.ts and test/workbench-inspector*.test.ts stay verbatim and green.
acceptance_criteria:
Red-first: test/workbench-observation-aggregates.test.ts fails before aggregate()/aggregateStats() exist. All quotes are from docs/workbench in the rig (branch workbench/implementation-program).

A1 Brute-force equality (falsifier). A seeded deterministic fixture (no Date.now()/Math.random() in the measured path, same rules as the header of test/helpers/perf-fixtures.ts) builds >= 500 nodes with grouping and ownership edges up to depth 8 including diamonds, plus dependency/causation/hypothesis edges; after every batch of status/interval/freshness mutations and edge additions, aggregate(key) for every key deep-equals an independent brute-force recomputation over grouping/ownership reachability with set semantics. Quote docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md § "Rendering pipeline": "Avoid O(allHistory) collapse per frame; maintain by-node last projection and ancestor aggregates incrementally." Quote docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md § "Truth labels and release gates": "Each major work package must have a falsifier: a negative test that would fail if a critical guarantee was quietly weakened."

A2 Only observed hierarchy counts. A dependency/causation/hypothesis-only fixture yields direct.children === 0 and descendants.counted === 0 for every key; adding a 'grouping' edge changes the parent's aggregate, adding a 'hypothesis' edge between the same pair does not. Quote docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Relationships are typed and provenanced": "lifecycle ownership (only if native producer confirms)", "grouping only (phase, display scope)", "inferred possible relationship (hypothesis; never treated as authoritative)". Quote docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-037: "Source-defined edges, observed edges and inferred links are distinguishable."

A3 Incremental propagation and depth cap. On a 10-level grouping chain, flipping the leaf from active to success increments descendants.byTone.success and settled at each ancestor within 8 levels, leaves the 9th and 10th ancestors unchanged with descendants.truncated === true and depthReached === 8, and aggregateStats().maxVisitedPerUpdate <= 8 for that flip. Quote docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-029: "Over 1000 nodes: render cost scales with visible slice and changed ancestors; no full historical-log fold per frame."

A4 Cycles and diamonds terminate. Grouping cycle A->B->A: both aggregates are finite (descendants.counted === 1 each), the test completes, depthReached <= 8; a diamond P->X, P->Y, X->Z, Y->Z counts Z once in aggregate(P) (descendants.counted === 3). Quote docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md § "Four views" Graph: "Cycles/unknown dynamic edges represented explicitly as \"references\" rather than rendered as a fake acyclic plan."

A5 Eviction and edge removal subtract. With maxNodes/maxEdges limits forcing FIFO eviction, discarding a counted child or evicting its grouping edge brings the ancestors' counts back to the brute-force value; stats() keeps the existing {nodes, events, edges} shape so test/workbench-observation-perf.test.ts toEqual stays green. Quote docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Derived view indexes": "Coalesce same-node repeated updates; do not rebuild entire history on each render."

A6 Measured intervals, no fabricated timing. Descendants with intervals give earliestStartedAt/latestEndedAt equal to the min startedAt / max endedAt of source intervals; a descendant with an open interval increments intervals.open and leaves latestEndedAt undefined; a descendant without an interval increments intervals.missing and sets trace 'incomplete'; criticalPath === 'unestablished' always, and JSON.stringify(aggregate) contains no numeric critical-path, token, cost or estimated field. Quote docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Aggregates and profiling": "Distinguish measured actual from estimated projected metrics. If dependencies or interval bounds are missing, suppress precise critical path claims and show \"incomplete trace\". Derive latency decomposition only with valid source intervals." Quote docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md § "Four views" Overview: "Critical path must be shown as *partial/estimated* when relationships/times incomplete."

A7 Freshness rollup. disconnect('furnace') raises descendants.stale to the number of non-current descendants; reconnect alone leaves it unchanged; a refresh() snapshot lowers it. title: W16-A: pure workflow_control decision module (grant+confirmed-ownership preconditions, observer-only and guessed-action refusal, requested/acknowledged/result receipt); Pi tool registration excluded
description:
Every `workflow_*` Pi tool and every `workbench:*` grant check lives in src/index.ts (hot, Sr. Engineer-owned), and native Furnace control would live in src/workbench/providers/furnace.ts (hot). W16's acceptance "compact bounded result and ACL" still needs a testable control core. Deliver it as ONE new source file and ONE new test file; register nothing.

src/workbench/control.ts (new), pure and provider-free:
- `interface NativeControlRequest { scope: ObservationScope; principal: { id: string; role?: string }; grants: readonly string[] | undefined; target: NativeRef; action: string; params?: JsonValue; invocationId: string; requestedAt: string }` (names follow docs/workbench/13 Host boundary `requestControl(req: NativeControlRequest): Promise<NativeControlReceipt>`; this bead implements the decision, not the host method).
- `decideControl(request, deps: { projection: ObservationProjection; now: () => string })` returns `{ decision: 'denied'; category: CapabilityErrorCategory; reason: string }` or `{ decision: 'permitted'; receipt: NativeControlReceipt }`.
- `NativeControlReceipt` phases are distinct and ordered: `requested` -> `acknowledged` -> `result`. Fields: contractVersion 'workbench.control/v1', requestId, principal, grant, policy (rule name), target, action, invocationId, ownershipConfirmationRef, requestedAt; `acknowledge(receipt, { acknowledgedAt, nativeAckRef })` and `settle(receipt, { outcome: 'completed'|'failed'|'cancelled'|'unknown'; nativeResultRef: string; settledAt })` return new frozen receipts and throw CapabilityError('validation') on out-of-order transitions or missing native references. The module never calls a provider, never mutates the projection, never fabricates acknowledged/result.
- Deny rules (first match wins, every rule has a test): grants undefined/non-array/non-string entries or any wildcard (`control:*`) -> authorization "unknown permission data"; grants containing only discover:/inspect:/observe: prefixes -> authorization "observer-only" regardless of action spelling (stop, STOP, terminate, __proto__); action not in the frozen per-provider allowlist (furnace: stop; claude-agent-sdk: interrupt; forge: cancel) -> validation "unknown action"; missing exact grant `control:<provider>.<action>` -> authorization; target key not in the request scope (different workspace/principal) -> authorization "cross-scope"; target lacking a projection `ownership` relation whose provenance.source === target.provider AND provenance.nativeConfirmationRef is a non-empty string (re-check both; do not trust the relation kind alone) -> authorization "no confirmed lifecycle ownership" (causation/grouping/hypothesis edges never qualify); destructive actions (stop, cancel, interrupt, kill, delete) without `params.confirmed === true` -> validation "operator confirmation required".
test/workbench-control.test.ts (new): one test per rule plus the phase-ordering falsifiers; no TTY, no providers, no network.
Out of scope: any edit to src/index.ts, src/workbench/providers/furnace.ts, src/workbench/claude-host.ts or other hot files; Pi tool registration; executing a native stop. If the worker finds registration necessary to satisfy acceptance, stop and return blocked.

title: VC-4/W13: Furnace observer projects Attempt nodes, Run->Attempt ownership edges and source intervals (additive)
description:
Gap: nothing in src/ calls ObservationProjection.relate(), so the W15 inspector's graph/overview/timeline never receive a real native edge; FurnaceObserver.projectionSnapshot() (src/workbench/furnace-observer.ts) emits a single Run node and flattens Attempt IDs into evidenceRefs with no Run->Attempt edge and no attempt interval, although FurnaceReading already carries attempts.items[{id,runId,workId,state,outcome,startedAt,finishedAt}] and the native attempts request ID.

Scope (atomic, additive, hot-file free): add FurnaceObserver.projectionTopology(reading) returning the unchanged Run snapshot plus one NativeSnapshot per returned Attempt (type 'attempt', bounded intervals from native started_at/finished_at only) and one 'ownership' relation Run->Attempt whose provenance.source is 'furnace' and whose nativeConfirmationRef is the attempts page requestId (the producer's own page asserts attempt.run_id === run.run_id). Partial pages produce no edges for the missing tail; stale readings throw like projectionSnapshot. projectionSnapshot() stays byte-for-byte compatible because src/index.ts:2560 (hot) consumes it; wiring projectionTopology into the Pi observe tool is a separate Sr. Engineer follow-up and is NOT part of this bead.

Files: src/workbench/furnace-observer.ts; test/workbench-furnace-observer.test.ts (or new test/workbench-furnace-topology.test.ts). Reuse the existing client() mock fixture style. Specs: docs/workbench/09 (Relationships are typed and provenanced; Acceptance/negative controls), docs/workbench/15 VC-4, docs/workbench/02 WB-025/WB-037, docs/workbench/10 Four views (Timeline).
acceptance_criteria:
Red-first tests in test/workbench-furnace-observer.test.ts (extend; never delete existing cases) or a new test/workbench-furnace-topology.test.ts, then minimal implementation in src/workbench/furnace-observer.ts ONLY. Hot files (src/index.ts, src/workbench/providers/furnace.ts, ...) must not be touched; keep projectionSnapshot() signature and behavior unchanged because src/index.ts:2560 consumes it.

A1. New additive method FurnaceObserver.projectionTopology(reading: FurnaceReading): { snapshots: NativeSnapshot[]; relations: FurnaceObservedRelation[] } where FurnaceObservedRelation is exactly the parameter type of ObservationProjection.relate. snapshots[0] deep-equals projectionSnapshot(reading); then one NativeSnapshot per reading.attempts.items entry with source {provider:'furnace', type:'attempt', id:item.id, scope:reading.source.workspaceRoot}, kind 'furnace.attempt.snapshot', node.type 'sdk-operation', statusText item.state (and outcome when present), trace {invocationId: <same as run>, correlationIds:{runId,workId}}, interval ONLY when item.startedAt exists and endedAt ONLY when item.finishedAt exists. No Work node is invented (no Work DTO is read); workId is a correlation id only.
   Quote: docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-025 "Workbench distinguishes Run/Work/Attempt, Forge operation and workspace basis, Claude session, HX coverage, RF provenance."

A2. Exactly one relation per returned attempt: {from: run ref, to: attempt ref, kind:'ownership', provenance:{source:'furnace', observedAt: reading.observedAt, nativeConfirmationRef: reading.source.requestIds.attempts}}. No 'dependency', 'causation' or 'hypothesis' edge is ever emitted by this method (test asserts every relation.kind === 'ownership').
   Quote: docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md section "Relationships are typed and provenanced": "lifecycle ownership (only if native producer confirms)" and "Store edge provenance with timestamp and source". Quote: docs/workbench/15-implementation-program.md section "Vertical cuts" VC-4: "Derived tree/timeline shows observed rather than invented edges."

A3. Partial pages: when reading.attempts.complete === false or attempts.unreadableCount > 0, relations exist only for returned items and the Run snapshot coverage stays 'partial'; nothing is synthesized for the missing tail.
   Quote: docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md section "Acceptance/negative controls" item 5: "Simulated missing relation; no fabricated dependency edge or precise critical path."

A4. Stale/disconnected reading (freshness !== 'current' or connection !== 'connected') throws CapabilityError category 'unavailable' exactly as projectionSnapshot does; no partial topology is returned.
   Quote: docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md section "Experimental projection implementation": "stale readings cannot refresh confirmed projection state."

A5. Integration proof against the real read model: apply snapshots via projection.refresh and relations via projection.relate on a real ObservationProjection; then projection.query({scope, parent: runRef, limit: 10}) returns exactly the attempt nodes; layoutInspector(...,{view:'graph'}) output contains 'ownership' and '[furnace]'; the timeline view prints a source interval for an attempt with startedAt+finishedAt and 'timing unavailable' for an attempt lacking started_at.
   Quote: docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md section "Four views" Timeline: "Never infer exact timing from text or assume clocks agree; note uncertain clocks or event gaps."

A6. Observer close still invokes zero control verbs (existing assertion pattern: stop/pause/resume/retry mocks have no calls) and no raw log line or redacted secret appears in any snapshot or relation (JSON.stringify(...) does not contain 'TOPSECRET').
   Quote: docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md section "Acceptance/negative controls" item 8: "Closing observer causes zero cancellation calls."

A7. Gate: ./node_modules/.bin/biome check --write on touched files clean; npm run typecheck clean (no any, no inline imports); ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run test/workbench-furnace-observer.test.ts test/workbench-inspector.test.ts green; record red and green commands in the delivered ledger line. Do not edit docs/TRACEABILITY.md (acceptance owner reconciles).

- test/helpers/detached-timing.ts:
  - pollFor(what, read, done, budgetMs = 20 s) re-reads every 20 ms (the old cadence) and THROWS DetachedTimingLapse '<what> exceeded its <N> ms wait timeout' at its budget, never a fall-through. holdOpen(ms) is for a window the test itself holds open.
  - markTimingLapse and marked re-label a failure carrying one of the product's two lapse sentences as DetachedTimingLapse '<site>: <bound> exceeded its ... timeout: <sentence verbatim>', with the original as cause; any other failure passes through unchanged.
  - raiseTransportLapse raises inspect's folded client-transport unknown for a lapsed socket timeout. A gone host (ECONNREFUSED/ENOENT) stays a reading the suites assert on.
  - refusalOf returns a refusal for comparison but rethrows a lapse (the judge reads no marker inside an AssertionError).
  - reportAfterCleanup settles every wait, runs the cleanup once, then reports the first lapse.
  - launchDetachedMarked and connectDetachedMarked are the marked twins of the product's launch and connect, with an injectable stand-in for the planted rows.
  - WAIT_BUDGET_MS 20000 (above the 2-5 s fixed counts it replaces, below the 30 s host-row timeout); HOST_HOOK_TIMEOUT_MS 30000 (a host-waiting hook's own lapse and its cleanup land before vitest's hook timeout).

THE MECHANISM (the U2 CURE example, taken whole): TREE_JUDGES = A1, A4, B1, C1, D1 (roster scan.treeJudges), held in the judged-set case to the pins whose own case source calls liveTree() and each of which records its view (A1 through recordOnce, the others through heldToA1). Each tree judge reads only its own VIEW: a structuredClone of the judged map and the readers list taken in its case (viewOf). A1 anchors its view (keys = the walk; textBlob = Git's blob id; reading = the compiler's own reading; NEW judged.readers: the readers list = exactly the judged modules whose own compiler reading holds the render command literal, read from the compiler readings, never from isReader or the view's readings). Every other tree judge digests its view at the END of its case (viewDigest: sha256 over every key in order, each reading with its textBlob, and the readers list), records the digest once (recordOnce: a read-only, non-configurable entry, so nothing that runs later - liveTree included - can replace or delete one) and asserts it equals A1's anchored digest (A4, B1, C1, D1 viewHeld, each +1 expect; witnesses gain viewHeld true); the records case holds all five digests to A1's, beside a constructed control (an empty view held against a scratch record seeded with A1's digest must record its own digest, not A1's, and must not reach VIEWS). judgedAnchor, walkAnchor, heldToA1, recordOnce, viewOf and viewDigest are const bindings (nothing reassigns them from the shared site). A pure, read-only reader of the rftsx program dispatch rule over the shared bead store (BEADS-2026-10-21.md:54@76bbbffd9d4a): ids, statuses and edges come only through two injected seams - bd show <id> --json (through the landed readBeadsWork, so every child status is that reader's sanitized label) and the bd dependents listing (dep list <epic> --direction=up --json), because bd 1.1.0-rc.1's show envelope of an epic carries no dependents (measured: bd show wb-4nut --json has dependent_count 0 and no dependents key while dep list wb-4nut --direction=up --json lists its 10 children; an epic without dependents prints [] rc 0; a missing id exits 1 with an error object). Program beads = the epics and their dependents; a child = a parent-child dependent carrying a wp: label (a ruling row is a record, never dispatched); only an open child is taken. A related premise inside the program holds the child until it closes, or, for a premise the store types decision, until the host witnesses its landed ruling/ADR text (landedRecords); a witness never satisfies a non-decision premise (no design doc is implementation). A blocks edge between two program beads is refused (CapabilityError validation, in a child or in an epic's dependents); a related edge outside the program holds nothing; an outside blocks edge holds the child only while open. A gated child (gates map) is ready only when its gate bead's appended notes carry exactly one whole line ruled ADOPT (ruled DEFER / ruled REJECT are the other verdict lines; zero or two read no-verdict); the title (whose creation form is the question "(ruled ADOPT or REJECT)"), description, status, labels and closure are never read. An unreadable store reads 'unknown (store unreachable)' with nothing listed or ready; an unreadable child or gate reads that status and is never ready; nothing ever falls back to a snapshot.

notes:
Full statement (title trimmed to bd's 500-character limit): [RF-FEDERATED-WORKSPACES-R3] No Pi adapter shall equate a workspace alias or filesystem path with a federated resource identity: Pi keys imported records by (workspace_id, backend_instance_id, resource kind/id, definition digest), treats the same workspace_id with a different backend_instance_id as a different authority, and treats source revisions as opaque per owner/stream — never ordering, differencing or merging revision counters across unrelated origins, backend instances or epochs — docs/programs/federated-workspaces-2026-10-18/03-protocol-and-storage.md:5@6a251bf73af5

Owner filing (2026-10-22, program-triage-2026-10-22; source federated-workspaces-2026-10-18/fw-alias-not-identity; adversarially verified 3-lens + dedup'd against the wb store).
Quote: "No implementation equates an alias or path with a global resource ID. Same W with different I represents a different runtime authority, as ADR-RFC-039 demands." — docs/programs/federated-workspaces-2026-10-18/03-protocol-and-storage.md:5@6a251bf73af5. Merged pins (same file+sha): :5 second clause "Source revisions are opaque per owner/stream; do not order revisions from unrelated B instances.", :50 (I02).
Authority: "D03 Stable identities include (workspace_id, backend_instance_id) plus resource kind/id and immutable definition digest. Friendly aliases are local, mutable names." (01-requirements-decisions.md:37) — Pi never substitutes a local name for identity nor orders opaque counters cross-origin.
Gating: none (standing); ResourceRef/ObservationRef fields ship with FW-02 (rfc-0txnl.2, BEADS-2026-10-21.md:14) and FW-04 (rfc-0txnl.10, BEADS:20). Shipped: no — OwnerResource (W,I) exists in domain/federation_boundary.py but no served envelope carries ResourceRef/ObservationRef.
Acceptance: (a) Pi identity/cache keys for imported records use (W,I,kind,id,digest); an alias rename leaves identity-keyed state untouched; no code path keys a resource by locator path; (b) same-W-different-I fixtures never collide in any Pi index nor share a revision ordering; (c) property test: comparators over observations from distinct (W,I) or epochs return typed non-comparable or refuse; no sort/merge key concatenates revision counters across origins.
Nearest wb: wb-0br, wb-973.8, wb-ae7u.
Not P0: standing posture, no live violation; identity fields gated on open FW-02/FW-04.

title: HXFS-PI-R1: a push-authority seat lands Pi's HyperUnix feedback entry on origin/main, verified from outside
description:
## Statement
A Pi seat holding push authority shall land Pi's HyperUnix feedback entry (commit `c52116840a`, path `new-feedback/2026-10-15-pi-workbench-sdk-find-preserves-incomplete-coverage-and-refuses-absence/`) on HyperUnix-CLI `origin/main` per that repo's producer contract (one finding per commit staged by path, `docs(new-feedback): <claim> (hu)` header with the six uppercase body sections, no model/vendor names, pushed `HEAD:main` by fetch-rebase-retry and never force), and shall verify the landing with `git merge-base --is-ancestor <landed-sha> origin/main` from outside the pushing clone. The re-delivered commit SHOULD additionally carry the retained probe `hx-coverage-probe.mjs` (and its stdout capture) beside README.md as artifacts cited by file name in an appended `SELF-REVISION` paragraph, without altering the entry's findings, grades, names or SHAs; if the writer declines, the commit body says so. A side-branch commit is not a delivery and is invisible to HXFS's main-only feedback census.

## Rationale
CONFIRMED (both refuter lenses regrade CONFIRMED). HX's producer contract defines delivery as landing on main: "The delivery is the push. A file on your disk is not feedback; a file the maintainers can read on `origin/main` is." (HyperUnix-CLI:new-feedback/README.md:115-116@d60f277a26) and "Verify the sha you pushed from outside; a push receipt is not a landing." (:143-144). HXFS cut 0 censuses new-feedback/ on main (01-feedback-evidence.md:7; 11-feedback-governance.md:5,:48) and values positive controls of exactly Pi's kind (11:34). Measured: `c52116840a` is not an ancestor of origin/main (rc=1 at d60f277a26, at 4baec37fdd, and at bcc23e3e02 on 2026-10-17); it exists only on `origin/feedback/pi-workbench-20261015-delivery`; origin/main is not an ancestor of it, so fast-forward of the commit itself is impossible and the rebase path (:139) yields a new sha. The first triage graded the duty COVERED via wb-kqx; HXFS is the HyperUnix program whose census this non-landing defeats (the HX half of RELEASE-CLAIMS-AUDIT.md:283's deferred five-row boundary). Probe sub-clause contested and resolved: the refuter's host fact is refuted (ls 2026-10-17 shows hx-coverage-probe.mjs, 765 bytes, plus hx-coverage.json at /var/tmp/pi-feedback-delivery-20261015/); the policy half is accepted, hence SHOULD and additive, never a rewrite (wb-jwc.2 twin rule). Priority: seat bd 2 — CONFIRMED delivery duty, not a runtime mechanism; same class as rf twin wb-jwc.1.

## Acceptance criteria
1. From a fresh HyperUnix-CLI clone or a detached worktree based on origin/main (never the shared owner checkout — README.md:118-120): `git show --stat --name-only <sha>` lists only paths under the entry directory. RED today: c52116840a lists 1 file (README.md) and its :23 cites a host path `/var/tmp/pi-feedback-delivery-20261015/hx-coverage-probe.mjs` against README.md:41-43 ("A finding cites its artifacts by file name.").
2. If the SHOULD is taken: the directory also holds `hx-coverage-probe.mjs` (byte-identical to the retained copy, 765 bytes) and `hx-coverage.json` (its stdout, 133,553 bytes), README.md gains one appended `SELF-REVISION` paragraph citing both by file name, and the README diff vs c52116840a shows additions only. If not taken: the commit body contains the sentence that the probe was not committed.
3. `git log -1 --format=%s <sha>` matches the `docs(new-feedback): <claim> (hu)` subject shape; the body contains each of PROBLEM, ROOT CAUSE, SOLUTION, TDD TESTING, RISKS AND URGENCY, PROVENANCE (README.md:123-126); the vendor-name grep over the commit prints nothing (README.md:126-127).
4. `sh tools/lint/feedback-layout.sh <sha>` exits 0 (README.md:14-15).
5. Before pushing, the writer re-reads `ls new-feedback/ | grep -i -- coverage` and `docs/feedback-dispositions.jsonl` (README.md:47-50,:148-153) and decides whether the on-main entry beginning `2026-10-16-run24-12-dogfood-hx-hx-find-states-one-fs-coverage-gap-as-completeness-incomplete-...` is the same mechanism; if yes, the directory is re-stamped `CORROBORATION-` with `**Corroborates:** <entry> — verdict STILL-TRUE` (prefix convention README.md:38-40; the `**Corroborates:**` format literal is README.md:80); either decision is recorded in the commit body.
6. Push is `git push origin HEAD:main` after `git fetch` + `git rebase origin/main` (README.md:139); no force flag appears in the shell transcript. Then, from a clone other than the pushing one: `git fetch -q origin && git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> origin/main; echo landed=$?` prints `landed=0`. RED today: rc=1 for c52116840a against d60f277a26, 4baec37fdd and bcc23e3e02.
7. Pi: docs/workbench/TRACEABILITY.md gains ONE appended row under `## Tool feedback delivery receipts` naming the landed sha, the outside-clone command and `landed=0`; lines :222-230@b3f9890 stay byte-identical; the wb-cax.1 ledger validator exits 0.
8. Negative: no step edits HyperUnix source, tests, docs/feedback-dispositions.* or another writer's entry (README.md:93-94); `git show --stat <sha>` names no path outside the entry directory.

## Pi surfaces
docs/workbench/TRACEABILITY.md:220-232 (append-only row; :226 byte-unchanged); wb-kqx notes (W20 channel record); external: HyperUnix-CLI new-feedback/2026-10-15-pi-workbench-sdk-find-preserves-incomplete-coverage-and-refuses-absence/ on origin/main.

(a) The fixture sentence: "Construct deterministic fixture with >=1000 nodes, >=100000 events, 1-100 active changes per tick, 5 nested groups depth, partial graph links, long Unicode paths and large transcript payload refs." (the docs text spells 1-100 with an en dash; quote it exactly, writing the dash with a doubled-backslash escape). (b) Seven "Measure:" bullets: "observer ingest events/s and projection memory", "p50/p95 reducer update and UI selector time", "p50/p95 layout render/navigate/resize time", "number of visible rendered rows vs total nodes", "terminal bytes per update (with line diff)", "recover snapshot/cursor latency", "Pi model tool response size under bounded queries". (c) The target/honesty sentence: "Proposed responsive target <=20ms per navigation/layout calculation on declared reference host, redraw <=4Hz live; no full 100k-event fold per redraw; report measured hardware/toolchain and outliers. No invented pass numbers." title: W12 fault gap: a non-read node() leaves no journal row until it settles (runtime.ts appends only after await callNode), so a kill after the provider side effect but before the host result, or after the result but before the append, leaves nothing for the resume tripwire and the next resume re-runs the effect live (duplicate effect); record a dispatched row before the call so a resume refuses that position as uncertain-effect until an operator reconciles it
description:
Gap (groomed by flywheel seat g2 round 5, run g2-work-r1; measured at rig origin/workbench/implementation-program e830ac2 = BOUNDARY base at groom time; anchors from git show e830ac2:<path>):

src/workflow/runtime.ts records a node() journal row only when the call settles: the live path appends at :1509 (ok true) or :1533 (ok false), both AFTER `const output = await callNode({...})` (:1482); the only pre-settlement append is the carry-forward of an already-refused entry (:1417). The admission at :1305-:1313 treats `nodeJournal.get(index) === undefined` as `{ kind: "live" }`. journal.ts:213 documents "Append one settled call. Failure to write is not failure to run." and its header promises that for any non-read effect class "the resume stops on it rather than re-running or silently replaying an effect the previous run already performed." That tripwire exists only once a row exists. Consequence: a process kill (or host crash) between the provider side effect and the host result, or between the result and the append, leaves NO row at that position, so the next resume admits the position as live and performs the effect AGAIN — the duplicate effect docs/08 forbids. docs/14 names both locations as required fault-injection points and no test exercises them (grep over test/ for "before journal append|before host result|dispatched row" returns nothing; test/workflow-effect-replay.test.ts covers only recorded rows; wb-tu1 covers a recorded row with an absent class).

Scope (atomic; W12 side-effect policy; owner ruling requested on the row shape before claim, see notes):
1. Red first, test/workflow-effect-replay.test.ts: a fixture capability with a non-read effect class and an exactly-once effect counter; the host seam throws/kills after the effect counter increments but before the result reaches the runtime (location "after provider side effect but before host result"), and a second variant settles the result but fails the append (location "after result before journal append", journal append seam injected to throw once). Today the resume re-runs the node: the counter reaches 2. Quote the counter in the red note.
2. Fix shape (proposed, owner may reshape): immediately before `await callNode` (after nodeSemaphore.acquire and the aborted/settled check) and ONLY when the current effect class is not "read" (including an absent class, mirroring wb-tu1's fail-closed reading), append a dispatched row `{ kind: "node", index, key: key ?? "", ok: false, capabilityId, effectClass (when defined), basis, dispatched: true }` through the same recordJournal seam. The settled row at the same index supersedes it on read (nodeJournal is a Map built last-wins per index, runtime.ts:719-721), so a completed run resumes exactly as today. On resume a dispatched row with no settled successor is refused at :1313 as uncertain-effect (the existing non-read refusal), the workflow_node event carries reconcile.state "pending", the hint names the producer and position, and the row is carried forward verbatim; workflow_reconcile inspect reports the position with outcome "unrecorded" (dispatched, never settled). Read-class nodes write no pre-call row: journals of read-only and agent-only workflows stay byte-identical (existing journal fixtures and assertions untouched).
3. isEntry (journal.ts:229) accepts the optional `dispatched: true` marker (anything else drops the line as mangled, as today); journal-compat.ts MIRRORS the runtime (never re-implements): a dispatched row classifies node-effectful with the dispatched marker in its census and no new class unless the owner rules one; test/workflow-journal-compat.test.ts gains the mirror case. Reconcile acknowledge/override over a dispatched row bind by entryDigest exactly as over a failed row.
4. docs/workbench/08 "Side-effect replay policy on resume" gains one sentence naming the dispatched row (owner-authored or in the same commit per the owner's ruling) and TRACEABILITY gains the row; node qa/workbench/status-ledger.mjs --strict exits 0 before delivery (12:10Z seat rule).

Open questions for the owner (recorded in notes): Q1 marker shape (`dispatched: true` vs a failure-shaped row with no marker); Q2 whether a FAILED pre-call append on a non-read node refuses the call fail-closed or keeps journal.ts's "failure to write is not failure to run" (today's policy); Q3 whether the Claude host's settled-agent prefix needs the same pre-call row for agents with non-read gates (out of scope unless ruled in).

Non-scope: no change to read replay (same effect class, basis and key, marked stale), no change to the reconcile grants (never mint reconcile:*), no change to agent prefix semantics, no change to the admission order ("Decided synchronously, before anything yields"). Files: src/workflow/runtime.ts, src/workflow/journal.ts, src/workflow/journal-compat.ts, test/workflow-effect-replay.test.ts, test/workflow-journal-compat.test.ts, docs/workbench/08 + TRACEABILITY (ruling-dependent). Serialized after wb-tu1 (same two source files; blocked-by). Tier: sonnet (multi-module, safety invariant).

Required outcomes: reconciliation/uncertainty/conflict; no duplicate effects, no invented PASS, no implicit mass cancellation." -> the resume refuses the position with CapabilityError category "uncertain-effect", the workflow_node event carries reconcile.state "pending" with the producer and position, and the operator reconcile journey (inspect -> evidence -> acknowledge/override) is the only way forward, exactly as for a settled non-read row. B6. docs/workbench/16-repository-refactor.md section "Compatibility feature control": "Ensure older journal format remains readable when supported" -> journals without the marker read exactly as today; journal-compat.ts mirrors the runtime with a mirror test. description:
Gap (groomed by flywheel seat g1 round 4, run g2-work-r1; measured at origin/workbench/implementation-program cd5aab7; src/workbench and src/index.ts are byte-identical at the b4ca4aa tip at filing; anchors from git show cd5aab7:<path>):

docs/workbench/09 section "Aggregates and profiling" requires latency decomposition derived "only with valid source intervals" and docs/workbench/11 section "Comparative experiment protocol" requires separating "model tokens, provider waiting, Forge build time, RF context time, external queue and overlay overhead when telemetry allows". Nothing in src/workbench computes any of it: git grep -i 'decompos\|latency' over src/workbench at cd5aab7 matches only a comment (capability-registry.ts:323). The projection already carries the inputs: ObservedNode.interval {startedAt, endedAt?} (observation.ts:10, :74), nativeRef.provider (:58), presentation.statusTone (:8), freshness and sourceConnectionState (:63-65), invocationId (:70); query() pages are bounded by maxQuery (default 100, :93) and report truncated. attention.ts (wb-6ze.4) measures OPEN intervals against a caller clock and a dependency-chain critical path; timeline.ts renders lanes; neither sums or attributes closed time by provider. designer.ts compareWorkflowRuns (:217) consumes CompareRun.metrics: readonly MeasuredMetric[] (:179, :185), but the registered workflow_compare tool fills metrics: [] (src/index.ts:2554), so every comparison today reports verdict unknown for want of a measured source (docs/11 section "Experimental read-only source tools": "Missing native measured metrics yields unknown, not a claimed optimization.").

Scope (atomic, pure, hot-file free): ONE new module src/workbench/latency.ts and ONE new test test/workbench-latency.test.ts.
- Export LATENCY_CONTRACT = "workbench.latency-decomposition/v1" (a new single-carrier literal; wb-cax.8's rule), a frozen LATENCY_CLASSES ["model", "build", "context", "queue", "query", "host", "other"] and a frozen provider map {claude-agent-sdk: model, forge: build, reactivefiber: context, furnace: queue, hyperunix: query, pi-workflow: host}; any other provider is "other" (never a guess from a title or kind).
- selectLatencyDecomposition(projection: Pick<ObservationProjection, "query">, input: {scope; invocationId; limit?: 1..100 default 100; usage?: readonly {source: NativeRef; inputTokens: number; outputTokens: number; evidenceRefs: readonly string[]}[]}) -> LatencyDecomposition {contract; basis: "observed"; invocationId; examined {nodes, truncated}; wall: {measured: true; ms; from: "root-interval"} | {measured: false; reasons}; components: one entry per class {class; providers (sorted, sanitized, bounded to 64 chars); nodes; intervals {closed, open, missing}; busyMs (sum of closed intervals); unionMs (union of closed intervals so concurrency never double-counts); measured: boolean; reasons}; waiting: {nodes; reasons: ["single-interval-per-node"]} (the projection holds one interval per node, so a waiting/executing split is unknown with that reason, never estimated); tokens: {measured: true; input; output; sources} only from supplied usage whose source matches an examined node's nativeRef, else {measured: false; reasons: ["no-native-usage"]}; overhead: {measured: true; ms} = wall minus the union of every component's closed intervals ONLY when wall is measured, examined.truncated is false and every examined interval is closed, else {measured: false; reasons}; caveat: one frozen constant stating closed source intervals only and unreconciled cross-provider clocks}. Reasons come from a frozen vocabulary (page-truncated, open-intervals, missing-intervals, no-root-interval, no-native-usage, single-interval-per-node).
- Export toMeasuredMetrics(report, {subjectBasis; freshness}) -> MeasuredMetric[] (designer.ts:179 shape; names latency.<class>.unionMs, latency.<class>.busyMs, latency.wall.ms, latency.overhead.ms; unit "ms"; source = the invocation's root nativeRef; coverage "complete" only when examined.truncated is false and the component's intervals.open + missing === 0, "partial" when some intervals are open or missing, "unknown" when nothing was measured; evidenceRefs from the examined nodes, bounded) so a caller can feed compareWorkflowRuns without any edit to designer.ts.
- Mirror attention.ts: refuse a bad limit with CapabilityError("validation", ...); re-check scope and invocationId on every page row (attention.ts:281); the wall comes from the examined node of presentation.type "workflow" for the invocation (the root) and only when its interval is closed; no clock, no Date.now, no Math.random; an interval whose instant is not a bounded timezone-qualified ISO-8601 string counts as missing; provider strings pass the shared sanitizers in src/workbench/redaction.ts (stripUnsafeText today; the single exported display helper once wb-952's respin lands) and a 64-char bound before they appear in output; no raw payloads, titles or evidence bodies in the report.

Non-scope: designer.ts, attention.ts, timeline.ts, observation.ts, src/index.ts and any Pi tool or dialog wiring (the workflow_compare reply builder is wb-69g.7; the metrics hookup into the registered tool is a later index.ts wiring bead under the BOUNDARY 12:25Z serialization rule); no estimate of a waiting/executing split; no critical path (attention.ts owns it); no token derivation from anything but supplied native usage.

All quotes are from docs/workbench in the rig at origin/workbench/implementation-program cd5aab7 (identical at b4ca4aa). Red-first: test/workbench-latency.test.ts fails before src/workbench/latency.ts exists.
L1. docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md section "Aggregates and profiling": "Distinguish measured actual from estimated projected metrics." and "Derive latency decomposition only with valid source intervals." -> only closed intervals (both bounds valid ISO instants) contribute to busyMs and unionMs; an open interval and a missing or malformed one are counted under intervals.open / intervals.missing and never summed; a static assertion proves the module source contains neither Date.now nor Math.random nor a now parameter.
L2. docs/workbench/11-designer-and-operator.md section "Comparative experiment protocol": "Separate model tokens, provider waiting, Forge build time, RF context time, external queue and overlay overhead when telemetry allows." -> a fixture with claude-agent-sdk, forge, reactivefiber, furnace and hyperunix nodes yields one component per class with providers listed, and unionMs < busyMs when two same-class intervals overlap; an unknown provider lands in "other"; waiting is reported with reason single-interval-per-node; tokens are measured only from supplied usage whose source matches an examined nativeRef (a usage row with a foreign source is ignored and the reason no-native-usage stands).
L3. docs/workbench/11 section "Comparative experiment protocol": "Decline precise claim if trace coverage insufficient; include raw evidence references." and section "Experimental read-only source tools": "Missing native measured metrics yields unknown, not a claimed optimization." -> overhead is measured only when wall is measured, examined.truncated is false and every examined interval is closed; a page larger than limit marks examined.truncated true, every component carries reason page-truncated and toMeasuredMetrics coverage is "partial" or "unknown", never "complete"; wall is unknown with reason no-root-interval when the root node has no closed interval.
L4. docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-038: "Versioned plan/execute/observe comparison uses immutable source and config digest references." and docs/workbench/15-implementation-program.md section "Vertical cuts" VC-6: "executes comparison with real native evidence; reports gains/confounders." -> toMeasuredMetrics rows satisfy designer.ts MeasuredMetric and, fed as CompareRun.metrics for a reference and a candidate run sharing one basis, compareWorkflowRuns reports the latency metrics as measured with reference and candidate summaries; with mismatched bases the existing confound behaviour is unchanged (designer.ts untouched, proven by git diff).
L5. Scope and bounds: a page row from another scope or invocation is dropped (attention.ts:281 precedent); a limit outside 1..100 is a typed CapabilityError validation refusal; the report for 100 nodes serialises under 8 KiB; provider strings carrying terminal escapes, bidi controls or zero-width characters are stripped and bounded through src/workbench/redaction.ts.
L6. Mutation table in the delivery note: summing open intervals, summing busy where union is reported, defaulting an unknown provider to model, measuring overhead on a truncated page, and minting tokens from node count each fail a named test.
