description: Gap (owner ruling on the wb-6hb.4 gate finding, measured at cd5aab7 with zod 4.6.7): for an input object carrying an own __proto__ (or constructor / prototype) key at any depth, the oracle in capability-registry refuses with the fixed text 'Prototype pollution key at invoke(...) input.__proto__.' and both node() surfaces refuse at the VM boundary, but the curated claude-tool surface (src/workbench/claude-capability-tools.ts) parses the raw input with a zod record schema first, which silently STRIPS the key, so the call is PERMITTED and the provider receives the stripped object. Graded Low-Medium: no authority escalation (the key never reaches the provider or the InvocationContext), but a breach of docs/06 'identical authorization and input contracts' across surfaces — a surface permitting what the oracle refuses is a widening by the falsifier's definition. Scope: scan the RAW tool input for prototype keys (own keys __proto__, constructor, prototype, at any depth, arrays included) before any zod parse, and refuse with exactly the oracle's text through the same sanitized reply path; share the scan with the registry oracle (one exported predicate, not a copy); add the cell to the wb-6hb.4 parity table and FLIP its pinned known-widening assertion in the same commit. InspectorModel (:10-18) carries only the optional evidence read side; there is no graph model field. wb-6ze.32 (open, sequenced after wb-6ze.27 per BOUNDARY 11:13:05Z) delivers the pure model src/workbench/graph-view.ts buildGraphView(reader, {scope, focus?, viewport, caps}) and EXCLUDES "src/ui/workflow-inspector.ts and all rendering/wiring", naming "graph-branch adoption is a follow-up that joins the wb-6ze.16/.21/.23/.26 workflow-inspector.ts serialization chain". This bead is that follow-up, mirroring wb-6ze.26 (timeline renders the lane model when InspectorModel.timeline is supplied) and wb-6ze.21 (overview renders an optional AttentionReport).

Scope (atomic, pure layout, red-first): add an optional `graph` field to InspectorModel typed from the landed graph-view exports (never re-declared here). When supplied, the graph branch of layoutInspector renders from the model only: one row per model node with provider/type/status tone; one row per typed edge with direction glyph, relation class and [provenance.source]; aggregate supernode entries rendered FIRST with their counted size; cycle and unknown-dynamic reference entries rendered as explicit 'reference' rows (never dropped, never drawn as an acyclic chain); a declared edge whose endpoint was never observed renders as a declared-dependency edge carrying an 'unobserved endpoint' marker, NEVER as unknown-dynamic (BOUNDARY 10:58:33Z rendering rule bound into wb-6ze.16: declared-vs-dynamic is the source-of-knowledge axis, observed-vs-unobserved is endpoint state); a model page flagged truncated renders a counted partial label and the footer keeps its incompleteness statement; the viewport row budget keeps the existing whole-block-or-counted-remainder rule; selection pointer, focus and filter semantics are unchanged. Every rendered string routes through the file's existing safe()/visibleWidth helpers (the shared sanitizers in src/workbench/redaction.ts). When `graph` is absent the graph branch output is byte-identical to today, so the existing graph cases in test/workbench-inspector.test.ts stay green by construction.

Excluded: dialog/host wiring that builds the model per redraw (owner's, as for wb-6ze.26/.21), src/workbench/graph-view.ts edits (wb-6ze.32 owns it; adopt its landed exports verbatim), src/workbench/topology-slice.ts, src/workbench/observation.ts, any production cap change, the hot files at groom time (src/index.ts, src/workbench/evidence-wiring.ts).

description:
Gap (groomed by flywheel seat g1 round 1, run g2-work-r1; measured at origin/workbench/implementation-program b44f1ce, the BOUNDARY base at groom time; line anchors from `git show b44f1ce:<path>`; SDK anchors from the pinned @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk 0.3.300, package.json:33).

The landed decision core src/workbench/control.ts lists the Claude producer's only control verb -- NATIVE_CONTROL_ACTIONS (control.ts:16-20) carries "claude-agent-sdk": ["interrupt"], and DESTRUCTIVE_CONTROL_ACTIONS (control.ts:22) includes "interrupt" -- and exports decideControl (:148), acknowledge (:186) and settle (:196) with the requested -> acknowledged -> result receipt phases (:55-70). The vendored SDK declares the matching native verb on its Query interface: sdk.d.ts:2882 `interrupt(): Promise<SDKControlInterruptResponse | undefined>` (type at :4668), documented as "only supported when streaming input/output is used" and "Older CLIs resolve to `undefined`". Nothing anywhere EXECUTES a permitted claude-agent-sdk interrupt decision: `git grep interrupt src/` finds no Workbench call site; src/workbench/claude-host.ts consumes the query as a bare AsyncIterable (ClaudeQuery at claude-host.ts:24; `for await (const message of query({ prompt, options }))` at :197) so the Query handle that owns interrupt() is never retained, and the host's abortAgent (claude-host.ts:275) is the runtime's own cancellation path (WorkflowHost.abortAgent, src/workflow/runtime.ts:205), not a workbench.control/v1 execution leg with receipts. The Furnace leg of this exact gap is wb-69g.3 (src/workbench/furnace-control.ts over an injected SDK seam) and the local-detached leg is wb-0kg.6 (ADMITTED by the owner); the Claude producer has no leg.

Spec basis: docs/workbench/06-capability-registry.md § "Optional inspect/observe": "Control actions are separate, explicitly registered by a provider with per-action preconditions and acknowledgements. No mandatory universal pause/resume/cancel methods." and § "Current experimental policy surface": "No universal observe/control methods are manufactured for producers." and "An effectful invocation that loses a usable answer remains uncertain and is not retried automatically." docs/workbench/12-security.md § "Authorization design": "Control decisions require native ownership/preconditions and, for destructive actions, operator confirmation." and § "Auditability": "Record authorized principal, capability contract version, logical invocation, target native ref, reason/policy, request acknowledgment and producer outcome for control operations." docs/workbench/13-contracts-and-config.md § "Host boundary": `requestControl(req: NativeControlRequest): Promise<NativeControlReceipt>`. docs/workbench/17-packaging-and-operations.md § "Error and degradation policy": "Expired control credentials -> deny action; preserving observation if allowed."

Scope (atomic, additive, hot-file free): ONE new source file src/workbench/claude-control.ts and ONE new test file test/workbench-claude-control.test.ts. The adapter consumes a decideControl result for target.provider "claude-agent-sdk" plus an injected session seam -- an interface the adapter DEFINES and the host will later satisfy, e.g. `{ interrupt(session: NativeRef): Promise<SDKControlInterruptResponse | undefined> }`, fake in tests exactly like the injected invoke seam in src/workbench/providers/furnace.ts and the wb-69g.3 pattern. It consumes the LANDED core (decideControl/acknowledge/settle) and never bypasses or reimplements it (BOUNDARY 07:49:42Z rule, applied to Furnace and local-detached verbatim). Register and wire nothing. Do not edit src/workbench/control.ts, src/workbench/claude-host.ts (retaining the live Query per agent session is the owner's host wiring), src/index.ts (HOT), src/workbench/evidence-wiring.ts (HOT), test/workbench-control.test.ts or test/workbench-host-contract.test.ts.

Behaviour to pin red-first (mutation-proof table mutant -> red test in the delivery note):
1. Verb allowlist: the only executable verb is "interrupt", proven by importing NATIVE_CONTROL_ACTIONS["claude-agent-sdk"] (never spelling a second copy) and cited against sdk.d.ts:2882 in the delivery note (the BOUNDARY 09:16:19Z citation rule applied to this SDK); any other action for this provider is a typed refusal and the seam is never called.
2. Denied decisions (every ControlDenyPolicy, including "operator-confirmation" for the destructive interrupt and "missing-exact-grant" for a revoked control:claude-agent-sdk.interrupt grant) return a typed sanitized refusal; the seam call count is 0.
3. Permitted decision -> the seam is called exactly once with the receipt's target; the adapter never retries (park-not-retry): a seam rejection or timeout settles outcome "failed" (or stays "requested" when the rejection precedes any acknowledgment) with a redacted diagnostic category, never a second interrupt.
4. Acknowledgment echoes, never minted: a resolved SDKControlInterruptResponse becomes the acknowledged phase with nativeAckRef derived from the real receipt and the still_queued uuid COUNT (uuids themselves sanitized, never raw); an `undefined` resolution ("Older CLIs") acknowledges with a named no-receipt marker, never a fabricated uuid.
5. Transport success is never domain verification: a resolved interrupt never yields outcome "completed" or "cancelled" by itself; the result phase is settled only from an observed terminal supplied by the caller (projection), otherwise outcome "unknown" with the docs/06 uncertain wording.
6. Every string that can reach an operator (diagnostics, ack refs, refusal text) routes through the shared sanitizers in src/workbench/redaction.ts (strip, redact, strip); byte-bounded.
7. Audit: every receipt phase carries the ControlReceiptCore audit fields unchanged from the core (control.ts:40-54); the adapter adds nothing to and removes nothing from them.

Out of scope: Pi workflow_control registration (src/index.ts), host retention of the Query handle (claude-host.ts), live SDK or claude-live tier, control.ts edits, Furnace/local-detached/forge legs (wb-69g.3, wb-0kg.6).

Files: src/workbench/claude-control.ts (new), test/workbench-claude-control.test.ts (new).

title: defect(wb-g1g.2): topology slice silently undercounts remainder and labels trace observed when projection maxQuery (prod 40) is below requested relationPage (default 100)
description:
Found by flywheel adversarial review run g1-r3 of branch machine/flywheel/wb-g1g.2 (commit 54e4dcc, gate receipt cmd_87383785df8f, which carried this as finding topology-slice-silent-page-cap-undercount, CONFIRMED medium, ownerRulingNeeded).

Defect: selectLinkedTopology silently undercounts the remainder and mislabels the trace "observed" whenever the projection's own relation-page cap (ObservationLimits.maxQuery) is below the selector's requested relationPage (default 100).

Mechanism (verified in code at 54e4dcc): src/workbench/observation.ts:624-625 relations() clamps limit = Math.min(input.limit ?? maxQuery, maxQuery) and reports no truncation; src/workbench/topology-slice.ts readSide() computes full = rows.length >= page against the REQUESTED page, so a page clamped below the request is indistinguishable from a complete read. The only guard is a doc comment on TopologyCaps.relationPage ("Must not exceed the projection's own page cap") — nothing enforces it, and the DEFAULT (100) violates it for the production projection, which is constructed with maxQuery 40 (wb-6ze.27 description, measured at 24e6015: src/index.ts:2380; W21 bench qa/workbench/grouped-fixture.mjs:36 also pins 40).

Independent runtime reproduction (review worktree at 54e4dcc, real ObservationProjection, vitest): new ObservationProjection({maxQuery: 40}); 45 observed dependency edges F->n00..n44; selectLinkedTopology default caps returned downstream 10 listed, remainder {count: 30, atLeast: false}, trace {label: "observed", reasons: []}. Truth: 45 observed matching edges, so the true remainder is 35 — 5 observed edges silently dropped, the count claimed exact, and completeness claimed. Control: caps {relationPage: 40} correctly returns remainder.atLeast true and trace incomplete-trace with reasons ["relations-truncated"]. This corroborates the gate seat's probe (10 listed + remainder 30 atLeast false, trace observed, 40 of 45).

Why this refutes wb-g1g.2 acceptance: B3 "neighbors beyond caps collapse to a counted remainder, never silently dropped" and the bead title's "missing relations never fabricated, incomplete-trace labeled". A trace labeled "observed" with an exact-claimed remainder while observed matching edges are dropped is a fabricated completeness claim, reachable through the intended consumer path (wb-6ze.24 computes the slice from ObservationProjection typed relations; production maxQuery is 40).

Suggested fix (red-first): falsifier first — maxQuery-40 projection with 45 matching edges under DEFAULT caps must yield remainder.atLeast true and trace incomplete-trace/relations-truncated (or an exact count of 35). Then either (a) adopt relationsPage {relations, examined, truncated, limitApplied} once wb-6ze.27 lands (consumer adoption is explicitly excluded from wb-6ze.27's scope, so no other bead covers this) and treat truncated || limitApplied < requested as a full page, or (b) require/accept the projection's effective page cap from the caller and clamp the requested page to it. Existing behavior when the page is honored (rows.length >= page => atLeast + relations-truncated) is correct and must not regress; never weaken the delivered tests.

description:
Gap (measured 2026-10-15T10:40Z against origin/workbench/implementation-program 24e6015, blobless clone, line anchors from `git show HEAD:<path>`): src/workbench/observation.ts:624 `relations(input: {scope; from?; to?; limit?}): Relation[]` clamps `limit = Math.min(input.limit ?? this.limits.maxQuery, this.limits.maxQuery)`, walks the outgoing/incoming/edgesByScope index and `break`s at the limit WITHOUT reporting it, while the sibling reads do report: `query()` (:704) returns `{nodes, examined, truncated}` and `events()` (:767) returns `{events, truncated, completeness}`. Production constructs the projection with maxQuery 40 (src/index.ts:2380, hot, not touched) and the W21 bench-only limits also pin maxQuery 40 (qa/workbench/grouped-fixture.mjs:36), while consumers request up to 100 (attention.ts:73 RELATION_PAGE = 100; workflow-inspector.ts:92-93 limit:100) or 40 (timeline.ts relationLimit default). Every consumer therefore guesses: attention.ts:141 "relations() reports no truncation and the projection caps each page at its own maxQuery, which this selector cannot see" and re-reads pair by pair under a 2,000-read budget (:75, :155-166); timeline.ts:44 "relations() reports no truncation, so a page capped below this limit cannot be told from a complete one" and :363 flags `truncated.relations` only when `incoming.length >= relationLimit`; workflow-inspector.ts:94-98 "a projection configured below 100 truncates silently, which relations() cannot report". Gate record: the wb-6ze.1 gate accepted "production maxQuery 40 < 100 makes relation-page truncation undetectable through relations(), so (partial) and relations partial fire only at 100"; the wb-6ze.6 gate relayed worker follow-up (3) "relations() reports no truncation, so a reader page cap below relationLimit cannot be detected". The Sr. Engineer approved this bead: BOUNDARY.md 2026-10-15T10:23:58Z "Approved for groom: ... relations() truncation-visibility bead" and 10:32:20Z "the four worker follow-ups are groom-approved".

Scope (atomic, additive, hot-file free): src/workbench/observation.ts plus ONE new test file.

- `export interface RelationPage { relations: Relation[]; examined: number; truncated: boolean; limitApplied: number }` and `relationsPage(input: {scope: ObservationScope; from?: string; to?: string; limit?: number}): RelationPage` on ObservationProjection. Same index selection as relations() (outgoing for `from`, incoming for `to`, edgesByScope otherwise), same scope-prefix guard, same exact from/to filters, same `Invalid relation query limit.` throw. `limitApplied = Math.min(input.limit ?? maxQuery, maxQuery)`. `examined` counts edges visited. `truncated` is true iff at least one further MATCHING edge exists beyond the returned rows: the walk looks one matching edge past the limit and stops. It never derives truncation from an index bucket's size, because a bucket may hold edges the exact from/to filter excludes.
- `relations()` keeps its signature and return type; it shares the private walk so `relations(input)` deep-equals `relationsPage(input).relations` for every input (falsifier below).
- Cross-scope `from`/`to` keys (prefix mismatch) return `{relations: [], examined: 0, truncated: false, limitApplied}` exactly as relations() returns `[]` today; a cross-scope caller learns nothing about edge counts.
- Read-only: `revision`, `topologyRevision`, indexes, edges and `stats()` are unchanged by any number of calls; no retained state is added.
- Export RelationPage so attention.ts, timeline.ts, the topology slice and the inspector can adopt it in follow-ups (a sibling adoption bead for attention.ts + timeline.ts is filed blocked-by this bead in the same groom round).

Files: src/workbench/observation.ts (additive method + exported type), test/workbench-observation-relations-page.test.ts (new). test/workbench-observation.test.ts may gain additive cases; its existing cases stay untouched.

Out of scope: consumer adoption (attention.ts, timeline.ts in the sibling bead; src/ui/workflow-inspector.ts relationsFor() :86-98 belongs to the wb-6ze.16/.21/.23/.26 serialization chain; wb-g1g.2 topology slice and wb-752.2 observe reply builder are in flight), any change to maxQuery or production limits, src/index.ts or any other hot file, Pi tool registration.

Falsifiers (mutation proof, run on a scratch copy and tabled in the delivery note): M1 `truncated := rows.length >= limit` (exact-limit page with no remainder must stay false); M2 `truncated := bucket.size > limit` ignoring the from/to filter (must stay false when the surplus is filtered out); M3 cross-scope key reports `examined > 0` (must stay 0); M4 relations() stops sharing the walk and diverges from `.relations` (deep-equal loop goes red); M5 relationsPage mutates revision (read-only case goes red).

All quotes are from docs/workbench in the rig (branch workbench/implementation-program, base d180dbb or later; 24e6015 at groom time). Red-first: the new test file fails on the base (relationsPage absent) before src changes. Line anchors are at 24e6015.

A1 reported truncation. docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md section "Experimental projection implementation": "Query indexes cover native references, invocation, typed relations, source basis, status kind, evidence, version and intervals. Event queries expose metadata and references without raw producer payloads. Source-qualified cursor retention loss is explicitly partial-gap." -- a projection constructed with {maxQuery: 2} holding 3 outgoing edges from key A answers relationsPage({scope, from: A, limit: 100}) with relations.length 2, truncated true, limitApplied 2; with exactly 2 edges truncated is false; under maxQuery 100 with limit 3 and 3 edges truncated is false and limitApplied 3; a property loop over limits 1..5 x edge counts 0..5 x {from, to, scope-wide} asserts truncated === (matching > relations.length) and relations(input) deep-equals relationsPage(input).relations.

A2 filter-aware, never fabricated from the index. docs/workbench/09 section "Relationships are typed and provenanced": "Store edge provenance with timestamp and source; Graph view styles each differently. Missing edges do not imply independence." and docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md section "Four-view viewport increment": "Missing edges, timestamps and evidence loaders are visible unknowns, never fabricated." -- with 5 edges A->C and 1 edge A->B, relationsPage({scope, from: A, to: B, limit: 1}) returns the single A->B row with truncated false (the 5 unmatched bucket entries create no truncation) and examined >= 1; every returned row carries kind and a copied provenance {source, observedAt?, nativeConfirmationRef?} and mutating a returned row never changes a later read.

A3 brute-force falsifier. docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md section "Matrix by subsystem" Observation row: positive proof "snapshots, dedup, cursor resume, provenance", negative control "event loss -> stale and unknown" -- over a seeded random edge set (200+ edges, 5 kinds, 2 scopes, duplicate from/to pairs) and 500+ random queries, truncated equals (referenceMatchingCount > relations.length) in every case, relations.length <= limitApplied, and the returned rows are the first limitApplied matching rows in index order (the same order relations() returns today).

A4 scope boundary. docs/workbench/09 section "Data retention and privacy": "Tenant/workspace boundaries apply at correlation queries, not just at individual SDK calls." -- a from/to key of another workspace or principal yields {relations: [], examined: 0, truncated: false} and relations() yields []; a scope-wide page for scope B never includes a scope-A edge and reports truncation only from scope-B edges; the ownership edge of another scope is never counted toward truncation.

A5 bounded walk. docs/workbench/10 section "Rendering pipeline": "Avoid O(allHistory) collapse per frame; maintain by-node last projection and ancestor aggregates incrementally." -- for an indexed from/to query, examined <= (edges in that index bucket) and the walk stops after the first matching edge past the limit (examined <= position of that edge), never edges.size; `npm run build && node qa/workbench/inspector-bench.mjs` and `node qa/workbench/inspector-grouped-bench.mjs` still exit 0 with their receipts cited in the delivery note.

A6 read-only. docs/workbench/09 section "Two-layer storage model" item 2: "Workbench materializes a bounded, rebuildable read projection for UI and Pi tool queries. It can cache snapshots/events with source/provenance, but is not a second authoritative Run/Work/Attempt or a global DB mandatory for execution." -- stats(), relationRevision() and the query() revision are identical before and after any number of relationsPage calls; JSON.stringify(relationsPage(x)) is identical before and after relations(x); the method is absent from the ingest/refresh/relate/markStale/disconnect/reconnect mutation surface.

A7 falsifiers and proof. docs/workbench/14 section "Truth labels and release gates": "Each major work package must have a falsifier: a negative test that would fail if a critical guarantee was quietly weakened." -- mutants M1-M5 from the description each turn exactly their named case red on a scratch copy while the base suite stays green; the delivery note tables mutant -> red test; test/workbench-observation.test.ts, test/workbench-observation-aggregates.test.ts, test/workbench-attention.test.ts and test/workbench-timeline.test.ts stay green untouched.

A1 docs/06 section "Optional inspect/observe": "Control actions are separate, explicitly registered by a provider with per-action preconditions and acknowledgements." -> executeDetachedControl handles exactly NATIVE_CONTROL_ACTIONS["local-detached"] = ["cancel","shutdown"], each proven against the DetachedCommand union (src/workbench/hosts/local-detached.ts:103-105, line cited in the delivery note, mirroring the wb-69g.3 argv.d.ts rule); any other action is denied by the core as unknown-action and reaches no client method (spy count 0).
A2 docs/12 section "Authorization design": "Control decisions require native ownership/preconditions and, for destructive actions, operator confirmation." -> both verbs are destructive: params.confirmed === true as an own data property is required by the core and never minted by the adapter; a denied ControlDecision of every policy (unknown-permission-data, observer-only, malformed-request, unknown-action, missing-exact-grant, cross-scope, no-confirmed-ownership, operator-confirmation) returns the typed denial and performs zero client calls.
A3 docs/11 section "First public Pi tools (proposed)": "returns requested/acknowledged/result distinct." and docs/08 section "State/event semantics": "Cancellation request != accepted cancellation != terminal cancellation." -> three distinct frozen receipts: requested from decideControl; acknowledged only when the host reply has accepted === true, with nativeAckRef "local-detached:<invocationId>:<hostInstanceId>:<verb>:accepted" built from the projected node and receipt, never from caller text; result for cancel: terminalConfirmed true -> outcome "cancelled", accepted but terminalConfirmed false -> outcome "unknown" (never cancelled, never polled or retried by the adapter), accepted false -> outcome "failed"; result for shutdown: unresolvedEffects false -> "completed", true -> "unknown" with the flag carried in nativeResultRef.
A4 A host refusal before acceptance (Authorization error because the launch permission list lacks the verb, or Unsupported/Invalid) leaves the receipt at phase "requested" and returns a typed sanitized refusal {category: "authorization" | "validation", diagnostic}; acknowledge() is never called. A transport failure after acceptance settles outcome "unknown" with a redacted nativeResultRef and the local-detached reconcile guidance; nothing is retried (docs/06 section "Registration and resolution": "No generic auto-retry").
A5 docs/10 section "Failure and deception defenses": "Cancel controls unavailable for observers without lifecycle authority." -> observe:/inspect:/discover:-only grants are denied observer-only by the core before any client call, re-proven with the new provider row; a target whose only relations are causation/grouping/dependency/hypothesis is denied no-confirmed-ownership.
A6 Never kills by pid: the module imports no node:child_process and calls no process.kill; asserted structurally like test/workbench-control.test.ts:370.
A7 Standing invariant: the reason, diagnostics and echoed host text route through src/workbench/redaction.ts; an adversarial reason with ANSI, zero-width characters or a bearer token never reaches a receipt or the client frame.
A8 Existing control tests green; a new test pins NATIVE_CONTROL_ACTIONS as frozen with the four provider rows and DESTRUCTIVE_CONTROL_ACTIONS containing "shutdown"; red-first, biome clean, no any, no inline imports, complete forge gate PASS, proposed-closure relay with the mutation table (each mutant -> red test) and the owner-ruling request stated.

Gap (measured 2026-10-15T10:00Z against origin/workbench/implementation-program 4ca6bd5): docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md section "Four views" requires the Timeline view to show "relative interval lanes grouped by owner/phase/provider, zoom and horizontal pan, observed waiting/executing/blocked periods and concurrency. Never infer exact timing from text or assume clocks agree; note uncertain clocks or event gaps." wb-6ze.6 (in progress, branch machine/flywheel/wb-6ze.6 at a937f53) delivers the pure lane model src/workbench/timeline.ts: TIMELINE_CONTRACT "workbench.timeline/v1", buildTimelineLanes(reader, request) -> TimelineModel { contract, revision, topologyRevision, origin {startedAt, basis 'earliest-observed-start'} | {startedAt null, basis 'none'}, span {ms, complete}, lanes: TimelineLane[] {key, label, basis 'ownership'|'grouping'|'provider', confirmed, rows: TimelineRow[] {key, nativeRef, title, tone, freshness, timing closed|open|unavailable, bar: TimelineBar {offsetCells, lengthCells, clippedLeft, clippedRight, openEnded} | null}}, concurrency {maxMeasured, basis 'source-intervals-only', countsOpenIntervals true}, notes: TimelineNote[] (codes clocks-may-differ, open-intervals-present, intervals-missing{count}, stale-rows-present, window-partial, relation-page-full, multiple-parents, rows-outside-viewport, phase-kinds-unavailable), truncated {lanes, rows, relations, window} } -- and its bead text says "inspector wiring excluded". InspectorModel (:9-15) carries projection, scope, invocationId, title, status only. No open or closed bead renders lanes: wb-6ze.16 is the details topology slice, wb-6ze.21 the overview attention panel, wb-6ze.23 the pane composition tiers, wb-6ze.15 the live pty receipt.

Scope (atomic, pure layout, hot-file free): edit ONLY the timeline branch of layoutInspector in src/ui/workflow-inspector.ts plus the InspectorModel type, and add ONE new test file test/workbench-inspector-timeline.test.ts.

- InspectorModel gains `timeline?: TimelineModel` (type import from src/workbench/timeline.ts; the host/dialog that builds it per redraw is the owner's wiring slice, mirroring wb-6ze.21's optional AttentionReport).
- When model.timeline is undefined the timeline branch output is BYTE-IDENTICAL to today for every (width, rows, ascii, zoom, pan, filter, focus) combination, so test/workbench-inspector.test.ts and test/workbench-inspector-window.test.ts stay green untouched.
- When supplied: a header line naming the contract-derived facts only (span ms or 'span unknown', complete/partial, concurrency.maxMeasured with its basis, origin basis); then per lane a header row (label, basis, 'confirmed'/'unconfirmed', row count) followed by its rows; each row draws its bar from TimelineBar cells only (offsetCells spaces then lengthCells glyphs, clipped edges marked, openEnded drawn open with a trailing open glyph), closed timing shows durationMs from the model, open timing shows 'open' and never 'timing unavailable', unavailable timing shows the model's reason; every row title and label passes the existing `safe()`/sanitizer path; every truncated flag that is true yields a counted remainder/notice line (lanes, rows, relations, window) and each note code renders as a fixed sanitized phrase (clocks-may-differ, intervals-missing with its count, ...). Rows honour state.filter and state.focused exactly as the other views do; the selected row keeps the pointer glyph; width is bounded through limitLine/truncateToWidth; the row budget and the trailing key-hint line are preserved; Unicode and ASCII tiers both covered.
- The renderer performs NO timing arithmetic of its own: no Date.parse, Date.now, zoom or pan maths in the branch when a model is supplied (falsifier below); it does not call buildTimelineLanes (the model is an input).

title: VC-1/W02-D: offline non-cancellation adverse-journey conformance for the Claude SDK host (inaccessible cwd refuses before any query; missing or schema-failing structured_output never success; success without session id refuses; absent modelUsage reports no tokens, never zero; non-abort stream throw after partial text is failed never cancelled, diagnostic redacted; unknown message discriminants never terminal; error-subtype results never success); test-only, src untouched
description:
Gap (measured 2026-10-15T10:00Z against origin/workbench/implementation-program 4ca6bd5; line anchors from a worktree checked out at that sha): docs/workbench/04-claude-agent-sdk-executor.md section "Tests" lists the negative matrix for the Claude host: "Negative: invalid model, absent credentials, malformed native output, stream error after partial text, aborted query, resumed unknown session, inaccessible cwd, invalid tool policy." and "No false successful tool or domain verdict after SDK result error". The cancellation half is covered (wb-a2g.2 landed F1-F9 in test/workbench-claude-cancel-faults.test.ts; wb-a2g.1 is the live tier), absent credentials belong to wb-cax.5 (D1), invalid model to the live tiers (wb-a2g.1/wb-a2g.6), transcript privacy to wb-dc0.1 and resume negatives to test/workbench-host-contract.test.ts (L4 :113, :183, :197, :208). The remaining non-cancellation journeys have typed code paths in src/workbench/claude-host.ts and NO test:

- :130-131 `if (!isAbsolute(config.cwd) || !existsSync(config.cwd)) return { ok: false, error: "Claude SDK cwd is inaccessible: ..." }` -- grep for "inaccessible" over test/ returns nothing.
- :235-236 `terminal.structured_output === undefined` with a declared schema -> "Claude SDK result is missing structured_output."; :238-239 `request.schema.check(...)` verdict !== true -> "Claude SDK structured output did not match schema: <verdict>" -- grep for either message over test/ returns nothing; the only structured_output fixtures are the success shapes at test/workbench-host-contract.test.ts:24 and :53.
- :229 success with no session id on init, assistant or result -> "Claude SDK succeeded without a session ID." -- untested.
- :83-91 `usage()` returns `{}` when `result.modelUsage` is absent or empty, so tokens/outputTokens stay ABSENT; docs/workbench/13 says "If the installed SDK lacks a field, omit it; no invented zeros or fake IDs." -- no test asserts absence (test/workbench-pi-client.test.ts:13 supplies modelUsage:{} but asserts nothing about tokens).
- :252-257 a throw from the SDK stream while the controller is NOT aborted -> `Claude SDK query failed: ${redactWorkbenchText(message)}` (ok:false, skipped absent) -- untested; the aborted branch (:254-255) is wb-a2g.2's F3/host-contract :134. Nothing pins that a credential inside the thrown SDK error is redacted before it reaches WorkflowSpawnResult.error.
- :199-212 the message loop recognizes exactly `system/init`, `assistant` and `result`; any other `type` is forwarded to onMessage and otherwise ignored, so a success-looking frame under an unknown discriminant must end as :216 "Claude SDK stream ended without a result message." (docs/workbench/13 "Key validations": "unrecognized SDK message version => diagnostic rather than silent success") -- untested; host-contract :152 covers only an empty tail.
- :226-228 a result with `subtype !== "success"` reports `redactWorkbenchText(terminal.errors.join("; ") || terminal.subtype)`, and `subtype === "success"` with `is_error: true` reports the redacted `result` text -- host-contract :123 covers one is_error shape; the error-subtype path, the empty errors[] fallback to the subtype label and the redaction of either text are unpinned.

Scope (atomic, test-only, hot-file free, src/ untouched): ONE new vitest file test/workbench-claude-adverse-faults.test.ts driving the REAL createClaudeWorkflowHost with query injected through ClaudeWorkflowHostOptions.query (the documented fixture seam, claude-host.ts:24 "SDK query injection exists for the fixture integration suite, not a fallback backend"), reusing test/helpers/claude-sdk-stream.ts from wb-a2g.2 where it fits. Journeys N1-N8 as listed above, each asserting the exact typed outcome, that `ok` is never true, that `skipped` is never set on a non-cancellation failure, that sessionId is carried when init delivered one and absent otherwise, that the Pi AgentManager path is never entered (the host imports neither AgentManager nor createAgentSession; assert the fixture query call count instead), and that every error string that originates in SDK text passes redactWorkbenchText (plant a bearer token and a JSON-quoted secret in the thrown message, the errors[] entry and the is_error result text; assert absence in WorkflowSpawnResult.error). N1 additionally asserts ZERO query() calls. N5 asserts `tokens`/`outputTokens` are absent properties (not 0, not null) and that the session entry recorded for a later resume carries no cumulativeTokens, with the positive control that a populated modelUsage sums as :88-90 does.

Mutation proof (local, on a scratch copy, never committed): M1 drop the existsSync guard -> N1 red; M2 drop the structured_output undefined check -> N2 red; M3 return ok:true when `!sessionId` -> N4 red; M4 return `tokens: 0` from usage() on empty modelUsage -> N5 red; M5 remove redactWorkbenchText from the catch path -> N6 red; M6 treat any message with a `result` field as terminal -> N7 red. Report which existing tests also catch each mutant.

Excluded: src/workbench/claude-host.ts edits of any kind (every path above already exists; if a journey proves a typed diagnostic ABSENT, file a follow-up bead instead of editing -- wb-a2g.5's reopen window stays with the owner), cancellation journeys (wb-a2g.2), auth (wb-cax.5), transcript privacy (wb-dc0.1), live tiers (wb-a2g.1/.3/.6), and every hot file (BOUNDARY 40a031a entry + src/ui/workflow-card.ts + src/workflow/reconcile.ts). acceptance_criteria:
All quotes are from docs/workbench in the rig (branch workbench/implementation-program, base 4ca6bd5 or later). Red-first: every N-case is written before any helper change and is observed failing or absent on the base. src/ untouched.

N1 inaccessible cwd. docs/workbench/04-claude-agent-sdk-executor.md section "Tests" lists "inaccessible cwd" among the negatives and section "Spawn algorithm" step 1 says "Validate request, agentType, model alias, effort, schema, tool policy, workspace materialization, requested isolation." -- a relative cwd and a non-existent absolute cwd each yield ok:false with the typed "cwd is inaccessible" diagnostic, the injected query() is called ZERO times, and the result is not marked skipped.

N2/N3 malformed native output. docs/workbench/04 section "Tests": "malformed native output" and "No false successful tool or domain verdict after SDK result error"; docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md section "Matrix by subsystem" Claude SDK host row: positive proof "schema result validated". -- with a declared schema, a success result whose structured_output is undefined yields ok:false "missing structured_output" and a success result whose structured_output fails schema.check yields ok:false "did not match schema"; in neither case does the partial object or the result text reach `text`, and ok is never true.

N4 session identity. docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-009: "Claude session IDs, input/output, tool events, native SDK failure and token usage are translated without invented values." and docs/workbench/13-contracts-and-config.md section "Agent execution contracts": "no invented zeros or fake IDs." -- a success result with no session_id on any frame yields ok:false "succeeded without a session ID" and no sessionId property is fabricated.

N5 usage without invention. docs/workbench/13 section "Agent execution contracts": "If the installed SDK lacks a field, omit it; no invented zeros or fake IDs."; docs/workbench/04 section "Spawn algorithm" step 4: "Never assume every message is final or every result carries usage." -- a success result with modelUsage absent and one with modelUsage {} both yield a WorkflowSpawnResult with NO `tokens` and NO `outputTokens` properties (asserted with `not.toHaveProperty`, never `toBe(0)`), and the recorded session carries no cumulative counters; the positive control with populated modelUsage sums input+output+cacheRead+cacheCreation exactly as src does.

N6 stream error after partial text. docs/workbench/04 section "Tests": "stream error after partial text"; section "Cancellation and steering": "Cancellation request != terminal acknowledgement." -- a stream that yields init and assistant text then throws while no abort was requested yields ok:false, `skipped` absent/false, error prefixed "Claude SDK query failed:", sessionId carried from init; a bearer token and a JSON-quoted secret planted in the thrown message are absent from `error` (docs/workbench/12-security.md section "Credential boundaries": "redact tokens from logs, UI, recordings and failure messages").

N7 unrecognized discriminant. docs/workbench/13 section "Key validations": "unrecognized SDK message version => diagnostic rather than silent success."; docs/workbench/04 step 4: "recognize official SDK message discriminants". -- a stream of init plus a success-looking frame under an unknown `type` (and a variant carrying `result`, `is_error:false`, `structured_output`) ends as ok:false "stream ended without a result message"; the unknown frame is still forwarded to onMessage exactly once; ok is never true.

N8 error-subtype results. docs/workbench/04 section "Tests": "No false successful tool or domain verdict after SDK result error". -- a result with subtype "error_max_turns" and errors ["<planted secret>"] yields ok:false with the redacted errors text; the same subtype with errors [] yields the subtype label, never an empty error string; subtype "success" with is_error:true yields the redacted result text; none sets ok:true or skipped.

Falsifiers and proof. docs/workbench/14 section "Truth labels and release gates": "Each major work package must have a falsifier: a negative test that would fail if a critical guarantee was quietly weakened." -- mutation proof M1-M6 from the description is run locally on a scratch copy and each mutant turns exactly its targeted case red while the base suite stays green; the delivery note lists mutant -> red test. The host never enters the Pi AgentManager path (docs/workbench/04 section "Tests": "Strict assertion that workflow agent() never calls Pi's createAgentSession/AgentManager under Claude backend"): assert on the injected query call count and the existing no-manager guarantee, do not add a new seam.

Gate. Complete forge gate PASS on the branch (FORGE_JSON=1 forge build --require-complete --no-replay --json); biome clean; no any; no inline imports; no existing test weakened or deleted; src/ diff empty.

comments.text: FINDING (ws-03, branch machine/flywheel/wb-a2g.7): the ~2.0 s is SDK-owned, NOT a Workbench wait. Abort -> SDK ProcessTransport.close() ends the child's stdin, then setTimeout(bqe=2000 ms) SIGTERMs a child still alive (@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk 0.3.300 sdk.mjs; unref'd timer, SIGKILL +5 s). The query stream and so host onSettled end when the child's stdout closes; the native claude child does not leave on stdin EOF mid-turn, so ack = 2000 ms + SIGTERM-to-exit (~2-3 ms) = the live 2002-2003 ms. Reproduced through the real createClaudeWorkflowHost: child ignoring EOF acks at ~2008 ms; child exiting on EOF at ~5 ms (same host code). Workbench-side code adds no wait (claude-host.ts has no timer). Tighter bound option: pass spawnClaudeCodeProcess to SIGTERM on abort; cost = bypasses the SDK's graceful stdin-EOF window and its process tracking (risk: truncated session transcript / resume lookup, orphan children on host exit), unmeasured live. description:
Gap (measured 2026-10-15T09:48Z, rig checkout a67bc36, file unchanged at origin tip 4ca6bd5): docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md section "Layout responsiveness" specifies three geometry tiers — "<80 columns or <20 rows: single-column compact tree; details as subview, no side-by-side graph." / "80–119: two-pane tree + details or timeline summary; scrollable pane cap." / ">=120: left hierarchy, center graph/timeline, right details when viable; cap width and height." — and "Resize preserves node selection, focus and scroll intent where possible." Measured in src/ui/workflow-inspector.ts layoutInspector (lines 239-330+): the only width-dependent branch is `width>=80` guarding one "Selected ..." line (:301, :316); every view (overview/graph/timeline/details) renders ONE column at every width and height, so the 80-119 two-pane tier and the >=120 three-pane tier do not exist, while the <80/<20 tier is already satisfied by construction. test/workbench-inspector.test.ts asserts 80x24 and 120x40 renderings with toContain only (:22-:107), so a pane layout at >=120 can keep them green. Related beads cover adjacent but different ground: wb-cax.9 (test-only geometry conformance: width-bounded lines, resize without stale rows; no pane semantics), wb-9x5.1 (landed 4267c11: bench measuring layout cost at 80x24/120x40 and resize), wb-6ze.16 (details renders the topology slice), wb-6ze.21 (overview renders the attention panel). Store dedupe (pane/responsive/two-column/three-column/Layout responsiveness): no bead implements the tiers.

Scope (atomic): pure layout in src/ui/workflow-inspector.ts (layoutInspector and private helpers) plus tests; the key reducer handleInspectorKey and InspectorState are unchanged (Tab still cycles state.view; state.view selects the center pane content and which pane carries the pointer). Dialog/host wiring excluded (src/ui/workflow-dialog.ts is HOT and already passes {width, rows, ascii}). No new projection methods: each pane consumes the same single bounded window page the current code fetches (one projection.window per pane at most), never raw event history.

Pane rules to implement (literal reading of docs/10; the owner may re-rule pane assignment — record any ruling in the delivery note):
- width < 80 OR rows < 20: the existing single-column rendering, unchanged.
- 80 <= width < 120 AND rows >= 20: two panes separated by one column of the existing box glyph family (ASCII '|'): left = the state.view rows (tree for overview, blocks for graph, lanes for timeline); right = the selected node's details rows (the same rows the details view renders, including the landed evidence and topology rows) when a node is selected, else the timeline view's header/summary lines. Each pane has its own row cap equal to the shared body height; rows past the cap end with the existing "… N more row(s)" notice (never silently dropped); pane widths split the inner width with the left pane never narrower than 40 columns.
- width >= 120 AND rows >= 20: three panes — left hierarchy (overview tree), center graph when state.view is overview or graph else timeline lanes, right details — when viable, meaning each pane keeps a minimum width of 36 columns after two separators; otherwise fall back to the two-pane rule. Pane widths are capped (no pane wider than 80 columns; surplus is left blank) and the total line count never exceeds rows.
- The header lines (title/status, view/count/follow, filter, focus, rule) span the full width above the panes; the key-hint line stays the last row.

All quotes are from docs/workbench in the rig (branch workbench/implementation-program, base 4ca6bd5 or later). Red-first: test/workbench-inspector-panes.test.ts fails before pane composition exists.

P1. Single-column tier unchanged. docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md section "Layout responsiveness": "<80 columns or <20 rows: single-column compact tree; details as subview, no side-by-side graph." -> for a fixture model with a selected node, layoutInspector at {width:79,rows:24}, {width:120,rows:19} and {width:30,rows:24} renders no pane separator and is byte-identical to the pre-change renderer's output captured in the red test for those geometries (the test pins today's lines for its own fixture, so the tier is proven unchanged rather than merely present).

P2. Two-pane tier. docs/workbench/10 section "Layout responsiveness": "80–119: two-pane tree + details or timeline summary; scrollable pane cap." -> at {width:80,rows:24} and {width:119,rows:40} with a selected node, every body row contains exactly one pane separator; the left pane holds the view rows (overview tree rows for view overview) and the right pane holds the selected node's details rows (native ref, status axes, evidence refs, and the landed topology rows from wb-6ze.16 when a slice is supplied); with no selection the right pane holds the timeline view's header/summary lines; a fixture with more rows than the pane budget renders the existing "… N more row(s)" notice inside the overflowing pane and never more than rows lines in total.

P3. Three-pane tier when viable. docs/workbench/10 section "Layout responsiveness": ">=120: left hierarchy, center graph/timeline, right details when viable; cap width and height." -> at {width:120,rows:40} with a selected node and view overview, body rows carry two separators: left = overview tree, center = graph blocks (the selected node's block first), right = details; with view timeline the center pane holds timeline lanes; at {width:200,rows:40} no pane exceeds 80 columns and no line exceeds 200 visible columns; at a width where three 36-column panes plus two separators do not fit the renderer falls back to the P2 two-pane rule (asserted at the boundary width computed from the exported minimums, which the test imports rather than restating).

P4. Resize preserves selection, focus and scroll intent. docs/workbench/10 section "Layout responsiveness": "Resize preserves node selection, focus and scroll intent where possible." -> the same InspectorState rendered at widths 79 -> 80 -> 120 -> 79 (rows 24/24/40/24) shows the pointer glyph on the same node ref in every geometry, keeps a focused subtree focused ("Focused on selected node and confirmed direct relations only" line present) and keeps the page offset (the "i/N" position in the view line) unchanged.

P5. Width safety in both tiers. docs/workbench/10 section "Layout responsiveness": "Unicode visibleWidth always used; guard wide CJK, combining emoji, ANSI codes, zero-width characters." and section "Proposed compact example": "For ASCII: +-|>, * running, x failed, ? unknown." -> with fixture titles containing CJK, combining emoji, embedded ANSI and zero-width characters, every emitted line has visibleWidth <= width at 80x24 and 120x40 in both the Unicode tier and {ascii:true}; the ASCII tier contains only ASCII separators and glyphs and no control bytes (shared sanitizer invariant).

P6. Bounded work, no new loads. docs/workbench/10 section "Rendering pipeline": "Avoid O(allHistory) collapse per frame; maintain by-node last projection and ancestor aggregates incrementally." and section "Four views" (Details): "Large content loaded only on focus." -> a projection spy records at most one window() call per rendered pane and zero calls to any event-history method during a three-pane render; no evidence loader or store.request is invoked by layoutInspector (store.get only, as today); the landed benchmark for wb-9x5.1 is re-run after the change and its measured p50/p95 at 80x24 and 120x40 are quoted in the delivery note (pass B stays within its own exit-1 rule; no production limit changes).

P7. Deception defenses preserved in every pane. docs/workbench/10 section "Failure and deception defenses": "STALLED vs WAITING vs STALE vs UNKNOWN must not be confused." -> the stale/unknown status text and the "Attention: stale/unknown is last-known state, not live progress." / critical-path lines (or the wb-6ze.21 attention panel when an AttentionReport is supplied) remain present in the overview pane at 80x24 and 120x40; tones and freshness labels are rendered identically to the single-column tier for the same node.

P8. Scope discipline: src diff touches only src/ui/workflow-inspector.ts; handleInspectorKey and InspectorState unchanged; dialog/host wiring untouched; all existing inspector tests and the wb-g1g.1/wb-6ze.16/wb-6ze.21 pins pass verbatim; biome clean; no any; no inline imports.

title: W22-M/W06: bounded in-flight admission in CapabilityRegistry.invoke (one registry-wide maxInFlight from an exported constant, FIFO wait bounded by the existing deadline and caller signal, typed 'unavailable' admission refusal distinct from the transport deadline, provider never called for a refused request, slot held until the provider settles, never auto-retry, counts-only admission snapshot for telemetry); runtime, worker and index.ts untouched
description:
Gap (measured 2026-10-15T09:48Z against origin/workbench/implementation-program 4ca6bd5; file lines from the rig checkout, unchanged at the tip): docs/workbench/17-packaging-and-operations.md section "Runtime and host requirements" requires "Streaming bounded by max in-flight node calls, backend admission and configured quota." docs/workbench/06-capability-registry.md section "Registration and resolution" requires "Establish max input/output sizes, execution deadlines, memory/event quotas and secret redaction." and its section "Current experimental policy surface" records what exists: "The host registry bounds JSON depth, bytes and wait deadlines." Measured: src/workbench/capability-registry.ts CapabilityLimits carries only maxBytes, maxDepth and deadlineMs (lines 58-65, validated at 197-203); invoke() (line 253) applies the deadline timer and the caller signal and nothing else; the only concurrency-adjacent bound anywhere is src/workflow/runtime.ts:690 `const nodeCap = 1000`, a TOTAL node-call count per workflow, so a script's parallel() over hundreds of node() calls dispatches every call at once against the native providers (forge/furnace/hx/rf CLIs and SDK clients) with no admission and no quota. Store dedupe (bd list --status all, terms in-flight/inflight/admission/quota/concurren/backpressure): no bead covers it.

Scope (atomic): src/workbench/capability-registry.ts plus one new test file. One registry-wide bound, no per-capability table (the owner can add one later); no edits to src/workflow/runtime.ts, src/workflow/worker-source.ts or src/index.ts (runtime/index.ts are HOT; the worker needs nothing because admission lives host-side where every node(), curated Claude MCP tool and Pi tool path already calls registry.invoke/inspect).

Design to implement:
- CapabilityLimits.maxInFlight?: number, validated exactly like the existing limits (safe integer >= 1, else CapabilityError("validation", "Invalid capability limit maxInFlight.")).
- One exported constant CAPABILITY_MAX_IN_FLIGHT (proposed 32) as the default; tests read the constant, never a literal (wb-oon/wb-cax.8 single-carrier precedent).
- Admission applies to invoke mode and inspect mode alike. When inFlight >= maxInFlight the call WAITS in FIFO order for a slot; the wait is bounded by the SAME deadlineMs timer and the SAME caller signal the call already has (no second clock, no new option).
- A call still queued when its deadline fires is refused with CapabilityError("unavailable", ...) whose message names admission and the bound (e.g. "Capability <id> admission exhausted: <maxInFlight> in flight after <deadlineMs>ms."); this is deliberately distinct from the existing CapabilityError("transport", "... exceeded its deadline ...") that means the provider WAS called. A call cancelled while queued keeps the existing "transport" cancellation family. In both cases provider.invoke/inspect is never called for that request.
- A slot is held until the provider promise settles, not until the caller is answered: a hung provider stays counted in inFlight after its caller's deadline rejection, so saturation is visible rather than hidden (honest backpressure; docs/06: a deadline "does not establish producer rollback").
- No automatic retry of a refused or queued-then-cancelled call (docs/06 "No generic auto-retry").
- registry.admission(): Readonly<{maxInFlight; inFlight; peakInFlight; admitted; refused; cancelledWhileQueued}> as a frozen counts-only snapshot for wb-cax.13's "provider call outcomes" telemetry; no ids, no provider names, no payloads.
acceptance_criteria:
Red-first: test/workbench-registry-admission.test.ts fails before CapabilityLimits.maxInFlight exists. Base 4ca6bd5 or later. All quotes are from docs/workbench in the rig (branch workbench/implementation-program).

A1. Bound exists and is validated. docs/workbench/06-capability-registry.md section "Registration and resolution": "Establish max input/output sizes, execution deadlines, memory/event quotas and secret redaction." -> new CapabilityRegistry({maxInFlight: 0}), ({maxInFlight: 1.5}) and ({maxInFlight: -1}) throw CapabilityError category "validation" with message "Invalid capability limit maxInFlight." (the existing limit-validation path); a registry constructed without the option uses the exported constant CAPABILITY_MAX_IN_FLIGHT and registry.admission().maxInFlight equals that constant (the test imports the constant; no literal).

A2. FIFO wait, not refusal, while a slot will free. docs/workbench/17-packaging-and-operations.md section "Runtime and host requirements": "Streaming bounded by max in-flight node calls, backend admission and configured quota." -> with {maxInFlight: 1} and a provider whose invoke resolves only when the test releases it, three concurrent invoke() calls reach provider.invoke one at a time in request order (release #1 -> #2 enters; release #2 -> #3 enters); provider.invoke call count is exactly 1 until the first release; all three callers resolve with their validated values; admission() reports inFlight 0, peakInFlight 1, admitted 3, refused 0 afterwards.

A3. Typed admission refusal, distinct from the transport deadline, provider never called. docs/workbench/13-contracts-and-config.md section "Workbench core types" (NodeCallResult): `{ kind: "rejected"; category: "validation" | "authorization" | "unavailable"; diagnostic: string }` and docs/workbench/06 section "Current experimental policy surface": "A deadline stops the caller's wait; it does not establish producer rollback." -> with {maxInFlight: 1, deadlineMs: 50} and the first call held open, a second invoke() rejects with CapabilityError category "unavailable" whose message contains "admission" and the bound; the provider was called exactly once (never for the second request); the message differs from the existing transport-deadline text ("exceeded its deadline"); a third call issued after the first is released succeeds (the refusal left no stale queue state).

A4. Cancellation while queued. docs/workbench/06 section "InvocationContext": "cancellation signal for current wait" -> a queued call whose context.signal aborts rejects with CapabilityError category "transport" (the existing cancellation family), provider.invoke count unchanged, and admission().cancelledWhileQueued increments by one; the slot order of the remaining waiters is unchanged (the next waiter still enters when the running call settles).

A5. Slot held until the provider settles. docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md section "State/event semantics" (via the registry's own deadline comment): a caller rejected by its transport deadline while the provider promise is still pending leaves admission().inFlight at 1 until the provider promise settles; a new call with {maxInFlight: 1} during that window is admission-refused (A3 path) rather than dispatched alongside the hung provider; after the provider settles inFlight returns to 0. Uncertain-effect semantics of the existing deadline path are unchanged (no new "uncertain-effect" category minted here).

A6. Inspect mode shares the bound. docs/workbench/06 section "Optional inspect/observe" -> registry inspect-mode calls occupy the same slots as invoke-mode calls (one held inspect blocks a second invoke under {maxInFlight: 1} and vice versa), proven both directions.

A7. Never auto-retry. docs/workbench/06 section "Registration and resolution": "No generic auto-retry; producer-specific adapters alone may reconcile native logical identities." -> after an admission refusal or a queued cancellation the provider is never invoked later for that request (count asserted after all other calls settle and after one macrotask turn).

A8. Telemetry snapshot is counts only. docs/workbench/17 section "Operations telemetry": "Report actual: ... provider call outcomes ..." and "Hide/redact prompt/tool bodies by default." -> admission() returns an Object.isFrozen snapshot with exactly the keys maxInFlight, inFlight, peakInFlight, admitted, refused, cancelledWhileQueued, all safe integers; serialized it contains no capability id, provider name, input or output text (asserted against a fixture whose capability id and payload carry a unique marker).

A9. No production behaviour change elsewhere: src diff touches only src/workbench/capability-registry.ts; all existing registry/security/node-contract/curated-tool suites pass unchanged; biome clean; no any; no inline imports; no hot file touched.

title: W22-K/docs-17: pure operations-telemetry report over the projection and supplied counters (active workflows with last-known-running+stale sub-count, Claude SDK sessions, provider call outcomes, event lag p50/p95 + clock caveat, dropped/late observations, projection size, visible rows, render p95, memory, SDK tokens, evidence coverage, ambiguous effects; each metric measured-with-source or unknown-with-reason, never default zero; counts and sanitized provider names only); wiring excluded
description:
Gap (measured at trunk 0ef5aeb, origin/workbench/implementation-program): docs/workbench/17-packaging-and-operations.md § "Operations telemetry" requires "Report actual: active workflows, Claude SDK sessions, provider call outcomes, event lag, dropped/late observations, projection size, number of visible rows, UI render p95, memory, token use from SDK, native evidence coverage and ambiguous external effects. Hide/redact prompt/tool bodies by default." grep -rni 'telemetry' src/ returns one OpenTelemetry comment (src/index.ts:714); no module aggregates any of these twelve quantities. The inputs exist: ObservationProjection exposes query() (src/workbench/observation.ts:477), events() (:540, completeness "complete" | "partial-gap") and stats() (:558 -> {nodes, events, edges}); ObservedNode carries kind, presentation.statusTone, freshness, sourceConnectionState, evidenceRefs and nativeRef (:56-76); ObservationEvent carries sourceTimestamp? and observedAt (:12-28); ingest() returns "applied" | "duplicate" | "out-of-order" (:261) but retains no counters; CapabilityErrorCategory (src/workbench/capability-registry.ts:39) names the provider outcome categories; the Claude host computes per-call token usage (src/workbench/claude-host.ts:83-89) but publishes no aggregate. wb-6ze.4 (landed a4cd2cf) set the pattern this bead follows: a pure, caller-clocked, bounded selector over one projection page with measured-vs-unknown labelling. wb-752.2 (in progress) builds the workflow_observe reply and may surface this report later; wb-cax.10 (owner-held) covers the other docs/17 residual (lazy init). No bead covers operations telemetry.

Scope (atomic, pure, hot-file free): ONE new source file src/workbench/telemetry.ts and ONE new test file test/workbench-telemetry.test.ts; wire nothing.
- export const TELEMETRY_CONTRACT = "workbench.telemetry/v1"; export const TELEMETRY_CLOCK_CAVEAT (event lag compares producer sourceTimestamp with observedAt; cross-provider clocks are not reconciled).
- export type TelemetryMetric<T> = { state: "measured"; value: T; source: "projection" | "supplied" } | { state: "unknown"; reason: "not-supplied" | "invalid-supplied" | "no-source-timestamps" | "no-events" }.
- export interface SuppliedCounters { providerCallOutcomes?: Readonly<Partial<Record<"returned" | CapabilityErrorCategory, number>>>; droppedObservations?: number; lateObservations?: number; visibleRows?: number; renderP95Ms?: number; heapUsedBytes?: number; sdkTokens?: number; claudeSessions?: number; uncertainEffects?: number } -- the host/dialog counts these (ingest results, provider outcomes, render timings, SDK usage) and passes them in; this bead defines the shape only.
- export function buildOperationsTelemetry(projection: Pick<ObservationProjection, "query" | "events" | "stats">, input: { scope: ObservationScope; invocationId?: string; now: string; limit?: number (default 100, max 100); eventLimit?: number (default 200, max 1000); supplied?: SuppliedCounters }): OperationsTelemetry -- a frozen report { contract; now; examined: { nodes; truncated; events; eventsTruncated; completeness: "complete" | "partial-gap" }; activeWorkflows: TelemetryMetric<{ active: number; lastKnownRunningStale: number }>; claudeSdkSessions: TelemetryMetric<number> (projection count of nodes with nativeRef.provider "claude-agent-sdk" and type "session"; a supplied claudeSessions is reported beside it with source "supplied", never merged); providerCallOutcomes: TelemetryMetric<Record<string, number>>; eventLag: TelemetryMetric<{ p50Ms; p95Ms; samples; unmeasured; providers: string[]; caveat: string }>; droppedObservations, lateObservations: TelemetryMetric<number>; projectionSize: TelemetryMetric<{ nodes; events; edges }>; visibleRows, renderP95Ms, heapUsedBytes, sdkTokens, uncertainEffects: TelemetryMetric<number>; nativeEvidenceCoverage: TelemetryMetric<{ withEvidence: number; examined: number }> }.
- Rules: projection-derived metrics come from ONE bounded projection.query({scope, invocationId, limit}) page and ONE bounded projection.events({scope, limit: eventLimit}) read; truncated and partial-gap flags are propagated into examined. activeWorkflows.active counts nodes with kind "workflow" and statusTone "active"; lastKnownRunningStale counts those with freshness !== "current" or sourceConnectionState "disconnected" (docs/09 § "Freshness and ambiguity" nuance). eventLag samples are observedAt minus sourceTimestamp in ms for events carrying both (negative samples clamp to 0 and are counted in unmeasured, as are events without sourceTimestamp); p50/p95 by nearest-rank over the sorted samples; providers = sorted distinct event.source.provider. Supplied metrics are measured only when the supplied value is a finite non-negative number (for the outcome record: every value finite non-negative), else unknown "not-supplied" / "invalid-supplied"; the report never defaults an absent counter to 0. now is the caller's clock (ISO-8601 with timezone; the module never calls Date.now); the projection is never mutated.
- Redaction: the report contains no node titles, status text, evidence ref strings, prompts, tool bodies or payload refs -- counts and provider names only; provider names pass redactWorkbenchText then stripUnsafeText (src/workbench/redaction.ts) and are capped at 64 chars; JSON.stringify(report) stays under 8 KiB for the maximum page and the test asserts it.

Out of scope: host-side counting (ingest-result counters, provider outcome counters, render timings, SDK usage aggregation live in src/index.ts, the dialog and hosts -- HOT or owner wiring; this bead defines SuppliedCounters only), inspector header or workflow_observe surfacing (wb-752.2), process.memoryUsage or any node:* read inside the module, docs or TRACEABILITY edits.

Specs: docs/workbench/17 (Operations telemetry; Error and degradation policy "Offline observation -> last-known state visibly stale; no fake terminal completion."), docs/workbench/09 (Observation event envelope; Freshness and ambiguity; Aggregates and profiling; Data retention and privacy), docs/workbench/13 (Agent execution contracts "no invented zeros or fake IDs"), docs/workbench/12 (Credential boundaries), docs/workbench/15 W22.
acceptance_criteria:
All quotes are from docs/workbench in the rig (branch workbench/implementation-program, base 0ef5aeb or later per BOUNDARY.md).
1. docs/workbench/17-packaging-and-operations.md § "Operations telemetry": "Report actual: active workflows, Claude SDK sessions, provider call outcomes, event lag, dropped/late observations, projection size, number of visible rows, UI render p95, memory, token use from SDK, native evidence coverage and ambiguous external effects." -> the report type has exactly these twelve metric fields (plus contract, now, examined); a fixture projection with 3 workflow nodes (2 active, 1 success) and 2 "claude-agent-sdk"/"session" nodes yields activeWorkflows {active:2, lastKnownRunningStale:0}, claudeSdkSessions 2 and projectionSize equal to projection.stats(); every field is either {state:"measured", value, source} or {state:"unknown", reason} (type-level exhaustiveness plus a runtime walk over the report).
2. docs/workbench/13-contracts-and-config.md § "Agent execution contracts": "If the installed SDK lacks a field, omit it; no invented zeros or fake IDs." -> with supplied undefined, providerCallOutcomes, droppedObservations, lateObservations, visibleRows, renderP95Ms, heapUsedBytes, sdkTokens and uncertainEffects are all {state:"unknown", reason:"not-supplied"}; JSON.stringify(report) contains no "value":0 for those fields; a supplied NaN, -1 or Infinity yields "invalid-supplied"; a supplied {returned:4, transport:1, "uncertain-effect":1} is measured with source "supplied" and every key preserved.
3. docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Observation event envelope (proposal)": "SourceTimestamp does not establish a total order across providers." -> eventLag over events from providers "forge" and "furnace" reports samples, p50Ms, p95Ms, providers ["forge","furnace"] and caveat === TELEMETRY_CLOCK_CAVEAT; events without sourceTimestamp are counted in unmeasured and never sampled; a window with zero timestamped events is {state:"unknown", reason:"no-source-timestamps"} ("no-events" when the window is empty); an events() read returning completeness "partial-gap" sets examined.completeness "partial-gap".
4. docs/workbench/09 § "Freshness and ambiguity": "A disconnected Furnace event stream must not make a previously RUNNING node permanently authoritative RUNNING; it becomes last-known-running + stale. Pi tool summaries must communicate that nuance." -> after projection.disconnect("furnace") an active furnace workflow node is counted in both active and lastKnownRunningStale; after a real refresh() snapshot restores the node, lastKnownRunningStale returns to 0 while active is unchanged; reconnect() alone does not clear it.
5. docs/workbench/17 § "Operations telemetry": "Hide/redact prompt/tool bodies by default." with docs/workbench/09 § "Data retention and privacy": "Avoid raw prompts/tool bodies by default; store reference/short redacted preview" and docs/workbench/12-security.md § "Credential boundaries": "redact tokens from logs, UI, recordings and failure messages." -> with node titles "Bearer abc123 secret", status text containing "api_key":"xyz" and evidenceRefs ["claude-message:0000"], JSON.stringify(report) contains none of "Bearer", "abc123", "xyz", "api_key" or "claude-message"; a provider name "fur\x1b[31mnace\\u200B" appears sanitized; JSON.stringify(report).length < 8192 for a 100-node/1000-event page.
6. docs/workbench/09 § "Aggregates and profiling": "Distinguish measured actual from estimated projected metrics." -> nativeEvidenceCoverage reports {withEvidence, examined} as two counts (no ratio or percentage is invented); a query page capped at limit 100 over 150 nodes reports examined.truncated true and the test asserts the coverage counts describe the examined page, not the projection.
7. Purity: buildOperationsTelemetry never calls Date.now (static grep of the module plus a Date.now spy), never mutates the projection (stats() and query() results identical before and after), returns deep-frozen output (Object.isFrozen on every nested object), and the module's import specifiers are limited to ./observation.js, ./capability-registry.js and ./redaction.js (static assertion).

- export const EVIDENCE_LOADER_ROWS: frozen table of exactly three rows {provider, requiredGrant, refKind}: {"claude-agent-sdk", "claude:transcript", "claude-message:<uuid>"}, {"furnace", "furnace:inspect", "native Attempt id listed on the owning run node"}, {"forge", "forge:inspect", "forge-operation:<operation_id>"} -- the docs/20 § "Producer mapping" table and nothing else.
- export function createEvidenceLoaders(input: { grants: () => readonly string[]; readers: { claude?: <landed claude-evidence.ts read function>; furnace?: <landed furnace-evidence.ts read function>; forge?: <landed forge-evidence.ts read function> }; owningFreshness: (scope: ObservationScope, nativeRef: NativeRef) => ObservedNode["freshness"] | "disconnected" | undefined }): readonly EvidenceLoader[]. Read EvidenceLoader/EvidenceContent/EvidenceRequest from the landed src/workbench/evidence-loader.ts (wb-g1g.1) and the reader signatures from the landed reader modules at claim time; never re-declare or re-implement either.
- Layer 1: a loader is constructed only when input.grants() (read once at construction) contains the row's requiredGrant as an exact string AND the matching reader is supplied; malformed or unknown grant entries are ignored (deny). Layer 2: every load(request) re-reads input.grants() and throws CapabilityError("authorization", ...) before touching the reader when the exact grant is absent.
- Routing: loader.provider equals the row provider; canLoad(ref) is the row's shape check only (uuid shape for claude-message, validated operation id for forge-operation, the furnace reader's own Attempt-id predicate); load(request) throws CapabilityError("validation") when request.nativeRef.provider !== loader.provider or !canLoad(request.evidenceRef) -- the store routes provider-first, the loader never guesses.
- Assembly: load returns the full EvidenceContent (docs/20 ruling 1): kind, provider, capturedAt, bytes, truncated, preview (the reader's lines passed through the idempotent shared sanitizers redactWorkbenchText then stripUnsafeText from src/workbench/redaction.ts; no new lines, no raw payload retained), sourceBasis only when digest-shaped (sha256:<64 hex> or the identity digest shape), otherwise omitted; freshness "stale" when owningFreshness reports stale, unknown, disconnected or undefined, "current" only for "current"; producerReceipt passed through when the reader supplies one. Reader failures propagate as CapabilityError with the reader's category (transport/authorization/unavailable/validation), never converted into a loaded entry; each loader exposes freshnessOf(request) so the store can label a transport failure against a disconnected source as transport plus stale.
- Anything else (hyperunix, reactivefiber, beads, unknown providers): no loader is produced, so the store yields unavailable: no-loader; the factory never fabricates a loader or a preview.
- Frozen outputs; no Date.now (capturedAt comes from the reader); no SDK imports; node:* imports only if the landed readers require them.

Out of scope: src/workbench/evidence-loader.ts (wb-g1g.1 owns it), the three reader modules (wb-6ze.8/.10/.11 own them), EvidenceStore construction and the load-evidence/abortAll dialog wiring (owner's wiring slice in src/ui/workflow-dialog.ts -- HOT), src/index.ts (HOT), hosts, grant settings parsing, any live SDK tier.

A loader constructed under a grant whose grants() later returns without it rejects load with CapabilityError category "authorization" and the reader spy records zero calls; "claude:transcript " (trailing space), "CLAUDE:TRANSCRIPT" and "claude:*" never satisfy the check (docs/workbench/12-security.md § "Authorization design": "Treat unknown permission data as deny.").
2. docs/workbench/20 § "Types": "`nativeRef` is required because evidence ref strings are not globally namespaced; producer routing keys off `nativeRef.provider` first, with `canLoad(evidenceRef)` as a shape check inside that producer only." and § "Owner rulings on the design conflicts" 3: "Loaders take the full request, not a bare ref; routing is provider-first." -> each loader's canLoad accepts exactly its row's ref shape and rejects the other two rows' shapes; load with request.nativeRef.provider "forge" on the claude loader rejects with category "validation" and calls no reader; the test enumerates all nine provider x ref-shape pairs and exactly three delegate to a reader.
3. docs/workbench/20 § "Producer mapping": rows "claude-agent-sdk session | `claude-message:<uuid>` | ... | `claude:transcript`", "furnace run | native Attempt id listed on the owning run node | ... | `furnace:inspect`", "forge operation | `forge-operation:<operation_id>` | ... | `forge:inspect`", "anything else | — | `unavailable: no-loader`, a visible unknown | —" -> EVIDENCE_LOADER_ROWS deep-equals exactly those three rows (a mutation test appending a fourth "hyperunix" row fails the pinned-table assertion); no loader is ever produced for a provider outside the table even when a grant such as "hyperunix:inspect" is present.
4. docs/workbench/20 § "Owner rulings" 1: "`loaded` equals the full `EvidenceContent` (kind, sourceBasis, freshness included)." and § "Types": "`sourceBasis` accepts digest-shaped values only." -> a reader result carrying sourceBasis "sha256:" + 64 hex is passed through; "main", "/tmp/x" and "sha256:abc" are omitted (never defaulted, never truncated into a fake digest); bytes, truncated, capturedAt and producerReceipt are copied from the reader, not recomputed; preview lines equal the reader's lines after the idempotent sanitizers and the factory adds no line (docs/20 ruling 2: "The double redaction in the sanitizer order is deliberate and idempotent." -- a reader line containing "\x1b[31m", U+202E or U+200B comes out stripped; an already-sanitized line comes out byte-identical).
5. docs/workbench/20 § "Refusal and freshness rules": "Stale or disconnected owning nodes label loaded evidence stale; a failed read against a disconnected source is transport plus stale. A loaded entry never upgrades projection freshness and never changes node status text or tone. Transport success never implies verification." -> owningFreshness "stale", "unknown", "disconnected" or undefined yields freshness "stale"; only "current" yields "current"; a reader CapabilityError("transport") propagates with the same category and loader.freshnessOf(request) reports "stale" for the disconnected owner; a forge reader result whose domain verdict is failed or partial is returned as its own kind/status, and the string "verified" appears nowhere in the module source nor in any emitted content under the fixture.
6. docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md § "Four views" (Details): "Large content loaded only on focus." -> createEvidenceLoaders calls no reader (spy count 0 after construction); only load() delegates, exactly once per call.
7. Negative controls: a request whose scope differs from the owning node's scope is rejected "authorization" without a reader call; the module never imports an SDK or node:child_process (static assertion on import specifiers); a request for a provider with no row (e.g. "hyperunix") finds no loader in the returned array (the store renders no-loader) and the factory exposes no fallback path.

description:
Gap: docs/workbench/17-packaging-and-operations.md section "Release checklist" item 8 requires "80x24, 120x40 and resize/SSH terminal tests pass." No deterministic conformance tier asserts rendering correctness at those geometries: wb-9x5.1 TIMES navigation/layout at 80x24/120x40/ASCII/resize but asserts no width, reflow or readability invariants, and wb-6ze.15 is the separate LIVE pty acceptance (blocked). Scope (atomic, test-only, src untouched, in the default gate):
- test/workbench-terminal-geometry.test.ts (new): drive the exported workflow card and four-view inspector renderers (the same compiled-surface entry points wb-9x5.1 benches) over a small deterministic fixture containing long Unicode/CJK/combining titles, zero-width characters and adversarial ANSI/OSC input.
- Geometry invariants at 80x24 and 120x40: every emitted line fits the column budget display-width aware (CJK wide cells, combining marks, zero-width stripped per the landed sanitizer rules); row count never exceeds the viewport; truncation is explicit, never silent overflow.
- Resize reflow: 120x40 -> 80x24 -> 120x40 mid-session re-render leaves no stale rows or artifacts, keeps the selection valid, and is idempotent for an unchanged model.
- SSH/dumb tier: the ASCII/dumb-TERM rendering path emits no raw ANSI/OSC control sequences and stays readable; adversarial input is neutralized via the shared sanitizers in src/workbench/redaction.ts (standing invariant).
- No timing claims (wb-9x5.1 owns timing); no live pty (wb-6ze.15 owns the live check); no src/ edits of any kind.

description:
